ideas.title: POS 'Exchange' at the till: return items and sell replacements on one ticket
ideas.prompt: Can you add proper exchanges to the POS? Today when someone swaps an item, the cashier has to refund it, finish that refund, then ring up the new item as a separate sale. I'd like an Exchange button next to Refund on the Orders screen: you pick what's coming back exactly like for a refund, then land on the normal product screen to add the replacement items (changing quantities etc. as usual), and the customer pays or gets back only the difference, on one ticket. The returned items must be credited exactly what a normal refund of them would give back. The new items must cost exactly what they'd cost in a fresh sale for that customer today, meaning their prices and our automatic promotions. Returned quantities still count against what's left to refund on the original ticket, and if the original sale was invoiced, the exchange gets invoiced too, like a refund would.
ideas.background: Odoo 19.4/20.0 Point of Sale is an OWL single-page app (addons/point_of_sale/static/src) that computes prices, taxes and totals in JS and syncs orders to the server. Refunds start on the Orders (ticket) screen. TicketScreen.onDoRefund (point_of_sale/static/src/app/screens/ticket_screen/ticket_screen.js:394-459) creates a new order with is_refund=true. It copies the selected lines with negative qty and keeps the original price_unit, discount and tax_ids, with price_type 'automatic' (getRefundLinesDetails 461-474). It also copies the original pricelist and fiscal position (414, 447-449) and then goes straight to the PaymentScreen. Refund orders reject positive lines: PosOrder.isSaleDisallowed (pos_order.js:441-443) is enforced in pos_store.addLineToOrder (939-946) with the message 'Ensure you validate the refund before taking another order'. Optional modules patch this flow. pos_discount implements global % or fixed discounts as separate discount-product lines. pos_loyalty implements promotions and loyalty rewards as reward lines. The feature is a third flow: one ticket that holds negative refund lines (linked through refunded_orderline_id) and normal positive sale lines, with the total equal to the difference.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin: grep -rni 'exchange' in point_of_sale/pos_restaurant/pos_discount/pos_loyalty static/src and models returns nothing relevant. isSaleDisallowed blocks any positive line on refund orders (pos_order.js:441-443). onDoRefund always navigates to PaymentScreen (ticket_screen.js:457-458). The only refund action in ticket_screen.xml is the Refund button (actionToTrigger.bind='this.onDoRefund', line 204). Upstream master (396a3df5be5b, 10351 commits ahead): master ticket_screen.js still has only onClickRefund/onDoRefund and still sets destinationOrder.is_refund = true (master lines 406-470). Master pos_order.js:394-396 has the same isSaleDisallowed. git log origin/master -i --grep=exchange on the POS static paths returns no POS exchange feature. There is no setting, preset or module for it: preset.is_return only flips every line negative.
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Add an 'Exchange' button next to Refund in ticket_screen.xml. 2) Implement onDoExchange by copying or parameterising onDoRefund. It uses _getEmptyOrder(partner) / addNewOrder({partner_id}), builds lines with getRefundLinesDetails, relinks combos, copies pricelist_id and fiscal_position_id from the original like refunds do, and calls setOrder. It then navigates to ProductScreen instead of PaymentScreen. 3) Either keep is_refund=true and relax isSaleDisallowed through a uiState.isExchange flag, or set is_refund=false. 4) Let the cashier add items through the normal ProductScreen (addLineToCurrentOrder). 5) The payment screen already handles negative or positive totals. 6) Write hoot unit tests in point_of_sale that use mocked products and check the order total equals new minus returned and that refundable qty is decremented.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: The returned items must be credited exactly what a normal refund of them would give back. / The new items must cost exactly what they'd cost in a fresh sale
traps.mechanism: A normal refund of a line from an order that had a global discount credits the discounted amount only because pos_discount patches TicketScreen.onDoRefund. That patch runs applyDiscount(value, type, destinationOrder) after the core refund (pos_discount/static/src/app/screens/ticket_screen/ticket_screen.js:7-16). Core getRefundLinesDetails copies only price_unit/discount (ticket_screen.js:461-474). (a) If the model writes onDoExchange by copying the core body, the patch never runs and returned items are credited at full price. (b) If it reuses onDoRefund, the exchange order gets a discount line, and pos_discount's model listeners (pos_discount/static/src/app/services/pos_store.js:13-43) re-run applyDiscount over every isGlobalDiscountApplicable line (pos_discount/static/src/app/models/pos_order_line.js:9-18, which excludes only tip and discount products) whenever a line of that order updates. Line creation triggers such an update through setFullProductName in PosOrderline.setup (pos_order_line.js:13-19) and the field setter in related_models/model_classes.js:120-122 -> _update index.js:530-560. So the old % lands on the replacement items, and the refund and new bases net out. Example: 2x50 with 10% global discount, exchange one for another 50. Expected +5 due. Both natural variants give 0.
traps.why_unsignposted: pos_discount's ticket_screen patch has no comments. The listener's only comment is 'Wait an animation frame before applying the discount' (pos_store.js:23). grep -rn 'exchange' finds nothing. Core onDoRefund/getRefundLinesDetails do not mention discount lines. Only pos_discount/static/tests/unit/components/product_screen.test.js:45-71 ('addProductToOrder reapplies the global discount') documents the listener behaviour, and it is in another module's test folder.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: The model's point_of_sale hoot tests do not install or load pos_discount data (discount_product_id, discount lines). Mocked orders have no global discount, so the totals assert new minus returned and pass.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Install pos_discount. Sell 2 x 50 with a 10% global discount (paid 90). A normal refund of 1 item shows -45 (baseline). Exchange 1 item for another 50 item: the ticket must show 5 to pay, with the new item undiscounted. Also read the diff for whether onDoRefund's pos_discount patch or the listener is addressed.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: The new items must cost exactly what they'd cost in a fresh sale for that customer today, meaning their prices
traps.mechanism: onDoRefund copies destinationOrder.pricelist_id = order.pricelist_id (ticket_screen.js:414). That is harmless for refunds because refund lines are price_type 'automatic' (471) and never repriced (getLinesToCompute pos_order.js:754-760). In an exchange every new line is priced from order.pricelist_id (pos_store.js handlePriceUnit 1031-1041), so an old manually chosen pricelist (for example 'Clearance -50%') or an outdated customer pricelist applies to the new items. If the model drops that copy, the destination order comes from _getEmptyOrder -> addNewOrder({partner_id: partner}) (ticket_screen.js:696-710). createNewOrder forces config.pricelist_id and the config default fiscal position even when partner_id is passed (pos_store.js:1243-1263). setPartnerToRefundOrder only calls setPartner when the order has no partner (ticket_screen.js:483-487), so the customer's own pricelist and fiscal position (setPartner -> updatePricelistAndFiscalPosition pos_order.js:578-584, 636-664) are never applied. The cashier cannot fix it by re-selecting the customer: selectPartner refuses on orders with refund lines (pos_store.js:2049-2057). Promotions restricted to pricelists follow the wrong pricelist too (pos_loyalty pos_order.js:493-500).
traps.why_unsignposted: createNewOrder has no comment about partner_id vs setPartner (the only comment in 1243-1290 is 'Meant to be overridden by pos_restaurant'). The pricelist copy in onDoRefund has no comment. Nothing states that refund lines are immune to pricelists while new lines are not.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit-test fixtures use the default pricelist and a partner without property_product_pricelist. The original order is created under the same default pricelist, so copying or not copying gives identical prices.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: (a) Customer with own pricelist Wholesale -20% (available in POS). Exchange any of their items for a 100 item, which must show 80. (b) Walk-in sale made after manually selecting a 'Clearance -50%' pricelist. Exchange it, and the new item must be at the normal default price. Natural code fails (a) if it does not copy the pricelist and (b) if it does.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: if the original sale was invoiced, the exchange gets invoiced too, like a refund would / (changing quantities etc. as usual)
traps.mechanism: Keeping is_refund=true (copied from ticket_screen.js:413, with only isSaleDisallowed relaxed) makes the frontend auto-enable invoicing (payment_screen.js:59-66 checks isRefund && lines[0].refunded_orderline_id.order_id.isToInvoice()). The backend then builds an out_refund for any is_refund order (point_of_sale/models/pos_order.py:886-888) and flips base-line quantities (pos_order_line.py:236-256, pos_order.py:237-246). A net-positive exchange (customer pays more) becomes a credit note with a negative total, which account.move._post rejects with 'You cannot validate an invoice with a negative total amount' (account/models/account_move.py:5789-5795), so invoicing fails at sync. Keeping is_refund=true also blocks every numpad edit on the order (product_screen.js:253-258) and sign-flips displayed line amounts through orderSign (pos_order_line_accounting.js:81-96). Setting is_refund=false fixes the backend, but then the auto-invoice rule, which is keyed on isRefund (payment_screen.js:59-66), silently stops applying.
traps.why_unsignposted: The move_type/qty_sign logic in pos_order.py has no comment about orders that mix sales and refunds. The frontend comment at payment_screen.js:60 talks only about 'refund orders'. Neither side mentions exchanges, so each half looks correct in isolation.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Frontend hoot tests never generate or post an account.move. Python tests would need the model to write a new mixed is_refund order with to_invoice, which the natural plan does not include.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Invoice an original sale to a company customer. Exchange its item for a more expensive one and validate. The invoice toggle must be on by default and the order must sync with a posted invoice (no 'negative total' error). Also check that a quantity can be typed on the replacement line.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: The new items must cost exactly what they'd cost in a fresh sale for that customer today, meaning their prices and our automatic promotions
traps.mechanism: New items are added through addLineToCurrentOrder. pos_loyalty patches it to call updateRewards (pos_loyalty/static/src/app/services/pos_store.js:369-460, call at 452). All reward maths runs over getOrderlines(), which includes the negative refund lines. _getDiscountableOnOrder sums line.prices.total_included of every line (pos_loyalty/static/src/app/models/pos_order.js:955-972). pointsForPrograms minimum-amount checks sum the rule lines including refund lines (514-580). getClaimableRewards uses the whole order priceIncl/priceExcl (760-761). Only _get_regular_order_lines excludes refunded lines (182-187), and it is used solely by _computeNItems (709). So an automatic '10% off the order' gives 10% of (new - returned), and a 'spend 50+' threshold is tested on the net, not on the new purchase.
traps.why_unsignposted: No comment in _getDiscountableOnOrder, pointsForPrograms or getClaimableRewards mentions refund lines. The one helper that does exclude them (_get_regular_order_lines) is not used by the discount computation, and nothing on the ticket-screen path points at pos_loyalty.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: point_of_sale unit tests do not load loyalty.program data. Exchange totals asserted without promotions are correct.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Create an automatic promotion '10% on the order'. Exchange a 40 item for a 60 item. A fresh sale of the 60 item gets -6, so the ticket should be 60 - 6 - 40 = 14. Natural code shows 18, or no discount for threshold promotions.

other_criteria: Exchange button only for paid/synced orders with refundable items; refundable quantity limits and combo relinking behave as in refunds
Returned quantities are reserved and decrease what can still be refunded on the original
Customer gets money back (negative total) or pays (positive total) on one ticket; receipt shows both returned and new lines
Original partner is kept on the exchange ticket
ideas.frontend_share: ~85-95% frontend. Changed files: point_of_sale ticket_screen.js/.xml, pos_order.js (isSaleDisallowed/exchange flag), product_screen.js (numpad block), payment_screen.js (invoice default), plus patches in pos_discount (ticket_screen/pos_store listener) and pos_loyalty (exclude returned lines from reward maths). A backend touch is only needed if the model decides to keep is_refund and fix move_type in pos_order.py.
ideas.risks: (1) The back-office already lets a manager open a paid order, 'Return Products' and add new lines to the draft refund (commit 95e63550b360 on master calls this an 'exchange scenario'), so a reviewer might say it is partly covered. It is not available at the till, which is what the prompt asks for. (2) Whether exchanges should be is_refund orders is debatable (Odoo's own back-office keeps is_refund), so the line-sign display should not be graded on its own. Only the invoice failure and the blocked numpad are tied to stated outcomes. (3) Traps E2 and E4 need the reviewer to configure a customer pricelist or an automatic promotion. (4) A model that greps for overrides of onDoRefund will see the pos_discount patch, though handling the listener correctly is still non-trivial.

ideas.title: Meal-voucher payment method that may only pay for food categories
ideas.prompt: We run a few delis in Belgium and lots of customers pay part of the bill with meal vouchers (Pluxee/Edenred cards). Legally those can only pay for food. Can you add that to the POS? Let us flag a payment method as a meal voucher and choose which POS categories count as food, subcategories included, and it must work on every till, even the ones set to show only some categories. On any ticket, the total paid by meal voucher can never be more than what the food on it really costs after every reduction: line discounts, the global discount button, and any promotion or loyalty reward. A gift card or eWallet used on the ticket is just another way of paying, it doesn't make the food cheaper. Vouchers never give change. Picking the voucher method pre-fills the most it may take, and the limit holds however the cashier pays, one-tap payment buttons included.
ideas.background: POS payment methods (pos.payment.method, loaded via _load_pos_data_fields at point_of_sale/models/pos_payment_method.py:133-134) have no notion of eligible products. Payment lines are added by PosOrder.addPaymentline (pos_order.js:470-489), which pre-fills getDefaultAmountDueToPayIn (pos_order_accounting.js:190-196). The payment screen edits amounts in updateSelectedPaymentline (payment_screen.js:168-211). Reductions in this codebase are rarely part of the item line. The pos_discount 'global discount' adds separate lines on config.discount_product_id, one per tax group (pos_discount/static/src/app/services/pos_store.js:52-133). pos_loyalty promotions add reward lines on reward.discount_line_product_id: order, cheapest or specific discounts per tax key (pos_loyalty pos_order.js:1134-1227), and free-product lines where the real product is only in a local field. Gift cards and eWallets are also negative reward lines, not pos.payment records. The feature adds a capped payment method whose cap is the cost of food after all reductions.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin: grep -rli 'meal.voucher|meal_voucher|titre.restaurant|ticket.restaurant|eligible' in point_of_sale, pos_restaurant, l10n_be_pos, pos_loyalty and pos_self_order returns nothing. pos.payment.method fields (pos_payment_method.py) have no category or restriction field. l10n_be_pos only sets the 0.05 cash rounding. Master (396a3df5be5b): git show origin/master:addons/point_of_sale/models/pos_payment_method.py | grep -i 'categ|meal|eligib|restrict' finds only ondelete='restrict' (master adds currency_ids, not eligibility). git log origin/master -i --grep='meal|voucher|eligib' on the POS paths lists only unrelated self-order/loyalty commits. No setting, module, plugin or labs flag covers it.
ideas.natural_implementation: Python: add is_meal_voucher (Boolean) and meal_voucher_categ_ids (M2M pos.category) on pos.payment.method, add them to its form view and _load_pos_data_fields. JS: PosOrder.getMealVoucherMax() sums line.priceIncl for lines whose product.pos_categ_ids intersect the selected categories or their children (PosCategory.getAllChildren/allParents), subtracts what voucher lines already pay, and takes min(eligible, remainingDue). Override PaymentScreen.addNewPaymentLine to set the voucher amount to that max. Clamp in updateSelectedPaymentline next to the existing showMaxValueError check. Possibly block validation in PaymentScreen. Hoot unit tests use a mocked order with food and non-food lines and assert the cap.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: never be more than what the food on it really costs after every reduction: line discounts, the global discount button, and any promotion or loyalty reward
traps.mechanism: Order-wide reductions are separate lines whose product is a discount product with no POS category. pos_discount.applyDiscount creates lines on config.discount_product_id per tax group over every isGlobalDiscountApplicable line (pos_discount/static/src/app/services/pos_store.js:52-133, pos_order_line.js:9-18). pos_loyalty 'order' discounts create lines on reward.discount_line_product_id per tax key (pos_loyalty/static/src/app/models/pos_order.js:1134-1227, applicability switch 1138-1145). Summing priceIncl of lines in food categories (the natural data source) therefore ignores them. Example: food 20 + magazine 20 with a 10% global discount has 36 due, so the voucher cap must be 18, but natural code allows 20.
traps.why_unsignposted: No comment on the payment path mentions discount or reward lines. getDefaultAmountDueToPayIn and the payment screen talk only about rounding. pos_discount and pos_loyalty never mention payment eligibility.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: point_of_sale hoot fixtures do not install pos_discount or pos_loyalty, so a mocked order has no discount or reward lines and the cap equals the food subtotal.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Install pos_discount. Ring food 20 + non-food 20 and apply the 10% global discount. Pick the voucher method: the pre-fill and the maximum typed amount must be 18.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: after every reduction: ... any promotion or loyalty reward
traps.mechanism: Promotions apply to particular items, but their lines do not say which in product_id. A free-product reward line has product_id = reward.discount_line_product_id, and the real product is only in the local-only field _reward_product_id (pos_loyalty pos_order.js:1396-1411; models/pos_order_line.js:34-40 'local: true'). 'specific' and 'cheapest' discount rewards target subsets of lines (_getDiscountableOnSpecific/_getCheapestLine 977-1107). The natural approaches are (a) ignore reward lines, because they are not in food categories, or (b) spread every reward line proportionally over the basket. Both give wrong caps. Example: 3 sandwiches at 5 with buy-2-get-1 free plus a magazine at 5 has 15 due, and food really costs 10. (a) allows 15 (so it pays the magazine) and (b) allows 11.25. Another example: '20% off magazines' must not reduce the food cap, but (b) lowers it.
traps.why_unsignposted: The comments in _getRewardLineValuesProduct/_getRewardLineValuesDiscount describe how lines are built, not that the discount product hides the discounted item. There is no helper that returns 'which items a reward line reduces'. _reward_product_id is a local underscore field declared in a different file.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked unit tests have no loyalty.program/loyalty.reward records. A model testing (b) would write expectations that already encode proportional allocation.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: With pos_loyalty, create (1) buy 2 sandwiches get 1 free and (2) 20% off magazines. Basket 3 sandwiches + 1 magazine: the voucher cap must be 10. Basket 2 sandwiches + 1 magazine at 10 with promo 2: the cap must be 10.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: A gift card or eWallet used on the ticket is just another way of paying, it doesn't make the food cheaper.
traps.mechanism: Gift card and eWallet redemptions are not pos.payment lines. They are negative reward lines on the program's discount product, created in _getRewardLineValuesDiscount (pos_loyalty pos_order.js:1175-1197) and kept last in _updateRewardLines (237). A model that fixes the previous traps generically ('subtract every negative or reward line from food') treats them as discounts. Example: food 10 + magazine 10 with a 10 gift card has 10 due. The cap must be 10, but the generic approach gives 5.
traps.why_unsignposted: The only hints are code comments inside pos_loyalty's reward builders ('These are considered payments...' 1175, 237). They sit off the payment-screen path and only help if the model studies those builders in detail. The reward line itself looks like any other negative discount line (is_reward_line=true).
traps.why_tests_miss_it: No gift-card programs exist in point_of_sale fixtures. A model's own test of the 'subtract reward lines' approach would assert the wrong value.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: With a gift card program, ring food 10 + magazine 10 and apply a 10 gift card. The voucher method must allow and pre-fill 10.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: the limit holds however the cashier pays, one-tap payment buttons included / Vouchers never give change
traps.mechanism: The obvious place for the cap is the payment screen, next to the existing max-value check. That check only caps when no cash method exists (payment_screen.js:186-200), so a non-cash line may overpay and the overpayment becomes cash change. Other paths add or grow payment lines without that code. Fast-payment buttons go action_pad.js:33-38 -> ProductScreen.fastValidate (product_screen.js:450-456) -> pos.validateOrderFast (pos_store.js:2487-2493) -> OrderPaymentValidation.setup -> order.addPaymentline with the full remaining due (order_payment_validation.js:31-33). Validate with no payment line auto-pays with config.payment_method_ids[0] (pos_store.js:2447-2465). Typing on a fully paid order adds payment_methods_from_config[0] (payment_screen.js:172-174). Adding a tip puts the tip on the selected payment line through setAmount (payment_screen.js:252-279). A cap implemented only in PaymentScreen.addNewPaymentLine/updateSelectedPaymentline is bypassed by all of these.
traps.why_unsignposted: getValidationOrderOptions has a comment about fast payment (pos_store.js:2451-2455), but nothing on the PaymentScreen path points to it. The existing showMaxValueError check suggests the payment screen is the place where limits live.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Component tests of PaymentScreen exercise only addNewPaymentLine and numpad input. Fast payment, auto first method and tips are separate flows the model would not mock.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Configure the voucher method as a fast-payment method (and as the first payment method). On a food + non-food basket, tap the one-tap button or Validate with no payment line, and add a tip with the voucher line selected. The voucher amount must never exceed the food cost and no change may come from it.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: choose which POS categories count as food, subcategories included, and it must work on every till, even the ones set to show only some categories
traps.mechanism: With 'Restrict categories' (limit_categories), the POS loads only the selected pos.category records and products (point_of_sale/models/pos_category.py:40-47, product_template.py:87-96). If a till shows only 'Sandwiches' and 'Soups', their parent 'Food' is not loaded. The eligible Many2many on the payment method then resolves to no loaded record, and product.pos_categ_ids[].parent_id / allParents (pos_category.js:19-33) cannot reach 'Food'. A client-side child-of check silently makes nothing eligible, or everything if an empty set means 'no restriction'. The child-of expansion has to be resolved server-side, or raw ids have to be used.
traps.why_unsignposted: The loading domain is in Python, far from the payment code. pos_category.js has no comment about partially loaded hierarchies.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit fixtures load the full category tree.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: On a config with limit_categories = {Sandwiches}, which is a child of Food, set the voucher eligible = Food. A sandwich must be payable by voucher.

other_criteria: Payment-method form gets a meal-voucher flag and a category selector
Pre-fill = min(remaining eligible food cost, remaining due) when selecting the voucher method
Several voucher lines (paper + card) share one cap
Non-voucher methods behave exactly as before; cash rounding (Belgian 0.05 cash-only) still applied to cash
ideas.frontend_share: ~80% frontend: payment_screen.js/.xml, pos_order.js or pos_order_accounting.js (eligible amount and cap), order_payment_validation.js (final gate), plus patches in pos_discount and pos_loyalty for reduction attribution. Small unavoidable backend touch: 2 fields on pos.payment.method + view + _load_pos_data_fields (and, for robustness, a server-computed child_of category id list).
ideas.risks: (1) Allocating order-wide reductions per item is somewhat open (proportional by value is the obvious reading). Reviewer tests should use the unambiguous cases listed: global %, free item, item-specific promo, gift card. (2) A strong model that reads pos_loyalty's reward builders closely can attribute rewards correctly. The 'one-tap buttons' wording will lead it to the fast-payment path. (3) It needs pos_discount and pos_loyalty installed for grading. (4) An OCA community module (pos_meal_voucher) exists outside the repo, so a reviewer might ask about prior art, although it is not part of Odoo.

ideas.title: 'Order again': start a new ticket from a past order for the same customer
ideas.prompt: Lots of our regulars (offices, caterers) order the same thing every week. In the Orders screen, add an 'Order again' button on any paid order that starts a new order for the same customer with the same items: same quantities, variants/options, notes and combo choices, so the cashier only has to tweak it. It must be priced exactly like a fresh sale for that customer today: their pricelist and tax setup, today's prices, and our automatic promotions applied, just as if the cashier had rung everything up by hand. Only real products come over: no discounts, promotion/reward lines, tips or gift cards from the old ticket. Anything we no longer sell (archived, removed from the POS, or currently snoozed) is skipped and the cashier gets told which items were left out.
ideas.background: Paid orders, including earlier sessions fetched with search_paid_order_ids/loadServerOrders (ticket_screen.js:921-965), can only be reprinted, refunded or invoiced. Rebuilding an order from them means creating an order for a partner and adding lines. Configured products and combos go through pos_store.addLineToOrder (911-992) and handleComboProduct (1047-1110). Pricing is order-level: pricelist and fiscal position on pos.order, applied for a customer by PosOrder.setPartner -> updatePricelistAndFiscalPosition. Promotions (pos_loyalty) are refreshed only from specific UI entry points.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin: grep -rni 'reorder|order again|orderAgain|duplicate' in ticket_screen.js/.xml and pos_store.js finds only product-sequence reordering (product_screen.js:131-142) and pos_restaurant table transfer. Self-order's order_history_page.js only lets you edit draft orders. Master: git show origin/master for ticket_screen.xml, ticket_screen.js, pos_store.js and order_history_page.js with grep -i 'reorder|order again|duplicate' gives no hit, apart from an unrelated comment at pos_store.js:2088. git log origin/master -i --grep='reorder|order again|duplicate order' lists only 'reorder products in config' and unrelated fixes.
ideas.natural_implementation: In TicketScreen add onClickOrderAgain(order). Create the order with this.pos.addNewOrder({partner_id: order.partner_id}), the same pattern as _getEmptyOrder. Loop over order.lines, skipping combo children and refund lines, and for each call await this.pos.addLineToOrder({product_tmpl_id, product_id, qty, attribute_value_ids, custom_attribute_value_ids, note, customer_note}, newOrder, {}, false) to avoid popups. Skip lines whose product is inactive, not available_in_pos or pos.isProductSnoozed and collect their names for a notification. Then this.pos.setOrder(newOrder) and navigate to ProductScreen. Unit test with a mocked paid order.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: priced exactly like a fresh sale for that customer today: their pricelist and tax setup
traps.mechanism: createNewOrder accepts partner_id in its create data but then forces order.setPricelist(this.config.pricelist_id) and the config default fiscal position (pos_store.js:1243-1263). The customer's property_product_pricelist and fiscal_position_id are applied only by PosOrder.setPartner -> updatePricelistAndFiscalPosition (pos_order.js:578-584, 636-664). ideas.title: Per-room 'Ignore @room' notification switch
ideas.prompt: Some big community rooms I'm in have admins who @room everyone several times a day and it's driving me mad. Can you add an 'Ignore @room' switch to a room's notification options (the room list menu and the room's Notifications settings)? When it's on, Element should treat messages in that room as if the @room simply wasn't there: no mention ping, no red badge. The message should still count like any normal message though, so in a room set to all messages I still get the usual notification, and in a mentions-and-keywords room I get nothing. If the same message also mentions me directly or has one of my keywords, I want the proper mention notification as usual. It has to cover @room from other apps too and sync to my phone. And don't break muting: a muted room stays totally silent whether I muted it before or after turning the switch on, and muting/unmuting never loses the switch.
ideas.background: Element Web implements per-room notification levels as Matrix push rules in apps/web/src/RoomNotifs.ts. Mute = a user-defined OVERRIDE rule with one room_id condition and dont_notify, created with rule_id = roomId (RoomNotifs.ts:133-158). 'Mentions & keywords' = a ROOM-kind rule with dont_notify (RoomNotifs.ts:176-182). 'All messages (loud)' = room-kind rule notify+sound (183-195). 'Default' = no room rule, so account underride rules decide (.m.rule.message / .m.rule.encrypted for groups, .m.rule.room_one_to_one which matches room_member_count == 2: test/test-utils/pushRules.ts:38-47, 139-146); RoomNotifs.ts:75-78 returns AllMessages whenever there is no room rule. @room pings come from server-default override rules .m.rule.is_room_mention (m.mentions.room, which Element sends: utils/messages.ts:54, 97) and legacy .m.rule.roomnotif (body contains '@room'), used for events without m.mentions. matrix-js-sdk evaluates rule kinds override, content, room, sender, underride (pushprocessor.ts:44-50, 392-415), and user-defined override rules sit right after .m.rule.master and BEFORE .m.rule.is_user_mention / contains_display_name / is_room_mention (pushprocessor.ts:123-137). Keywords are CONTENT-kind rules (Notifications.tsx:566, 619; reconcileNotificationSettings.ts:228-236). The feature needs a coordinated set of per-room override rules: an @room rule whose actions equal what an ordinary message would get at the room's effective level, higher-priority per-room exceptions for direct mentions and each keyword, all kept below the mute rule, and re-synced when the room level changes.
ideas.gap_evidence: At pin and at upstream HEAD a3f5be54 (2026-11-04): grep -rn 'IsRoomMention|AtRoomNotification|roomnotif' apps/web/src hits only the global settings page (pin Notifications.tsx:93, 302; HEAD Notifications.tsx:94-119, 326-328), renderer/pill.tsx:67 and VectorPushRulesDefinitions.ts:110-118. grep 'addPushRule(' hits only RoomNotifs.ts mute/room rules (148, 179, 185), the global keyword code (Notifications.tsx:619) and hooks/useNotificationSettings.ts:20. Room notification UIs offer only Default / All messages / Mentions & keywords / Off (NotificationSettingsTab.tsx:166-236, RoomListItemViewModel.ts:344-366). git log ee5d2609..HEAD -i --grep='@room|room mention|at-room|atroom' returns nothing; the only related commit since pin, 161aef320f 'Stop writing removed legacy mention rules from the Labs notification settings', is global. Settings.tsx has no per-room @room setting, labs flag or module hook.
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Add getRoomIgnoresAtRoom/setRoomIgnoresAtRoom next to setRoomNotifsStateMuted in RoomNotifs.ts, copying its pattern: cli.addPushRule('global', PushRuleKind.Override, id, {conditions: [event_match room_id == roomId, event_property_is content m.mentions.room == true], actions: [DontNotify]}), maybe plus a second rule matching content.body '@room'. The id is roomId or roomId plus a suffix; turning the switch off deletes the rule(s). 2) Read state from cli.pushRules.global.override. 3) Add a toggle to RoomNotificationContextMenu, RoomListItemViewModel and the shared-components room list menu, and to NotificationSettingsTab. 4) Unit tests mock addPushRule/deletePushRule and assert the rule body. This single dont_notify override shadows direct mentions and keywords, kills the ordinary notification in All-messages rooms, and goes wrong with mute ordering.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: If the same message also mentions me directly or has one of my keywords, I want the proper mention notification as usual.
traps.mechanism: A per-room override rule matching m.mentions.room is evaluated before every server-default override and before all content (keyword) rules (pushprocessor.ts:44-50 kind order; 123-137 UserDefinedRules placed before RuleId.IsUserMention, ContainsDisplayName, IsRoomMention, AtRoomNotification). So an '@room @me' or '@room <keyword>' message stops at the dont_notify rule, and .m.rule.is_user_mention and the content-kind keyword rules (Notifications.tsx:566, 619; reconcileNotificationSettings.ts:228-236) never run. Push-rule conditions cannot express 'and not mentioning me', so a correct solution adds higher-priority per-room override rules for user mentions (event_property_contains m.mentions.user_ids) and for each keyword (event_match content.body), with the right notify/highlight/sound actions.
traps.why_unsignposted: Nothing in Element discusses rule precedence. grep -rn 'is_user_mention|priority|before=' apps/web/src finds no comment on user override rules shadowing default rules. RoomNotifs.ts comments (75-80, 136-147) cover only mute versus room rules. js-sdk addPushRule (client.ts:7782-7798) has no docs on ordering. The neighbouring mute implementation is a one-rule override, so copying it looks complete.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Natural tests mock MatrixClient.addPushRule and only check that the expected rule was PUT. Even a test using a real PushProcessor only covers the cases the author thought of, usually a plain @room message.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Read the diff: is there only one suppress rule, with no higher-priority mention or keyword exceptions? Manual: turn the switch on, then from a second account with @room permission send '@room hi @me' and '@room <one of my keywords>'. Both must give a highlighted mention notification. A plain '@room hi' must not.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: The message should still count like any normal message though, so in a room set to all messages I still get the usual notification, and in a mentions-and-keywords room I get nothing.
traps.mechanism: A dont_notify override removes the ordinary notification in All-messages rooms. A [notify] override breaks Mentions & keywords rooms, because an override beats the room-kind dont_notify rule that implements that level (RoomNotifs.ts:176-182). So the @room rule's actions must depend on the room's effective level and be rewritten when the level changes. 'Default' rooms have no room rule (RoomNotifs.ts:75-78) and take their behaviour from the account underride rules (.m.rule.message or .m.rule.encrypted, versus .m.rule.room_one_to_one with sound when room_member_count == 2; test-utils/pushRules.ts:38-47, 139-146). The level can be changed from three UIs (RoomListItemViewModel.ts:344-366 via EchoChamber, NotificationSettingsTab, RoomNotificationContextMenu), or from another device.
traps.why_unsignposted: The enum name RoomNotifState.AllMessages suggests a literal level, but it means 'no room rule'; only an XXX comment hints at this (RoomNotifs.ts:75-77). No code ties any other rule's actions to the room's level, and NotificationSettings2 maps the one-to-one rules to 'DM' defaults (toNotificationSettings.ts:67-71), which hides the member-count semantics.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests build a room with one fixed notification level, or none, and assert that rules were created. They never change the level after the switch is on, and they never compare the result with what an ordinary message would get.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Set the room to 'All messages' and enable the switch; a plain '@room hello' from another account must produce a normal unread count and notification with no highlight. Switch the room to 'Mentions & keywords' without touching the switch; the same message must produce nothing. Read the diff for level-aware actions and for re-sync on level changes.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: a muted room stays totally silent whether I muted it before or after turning the switch on, and muting/unmuting never loses the switch.
traps.mechanism: (a) Collision: Element's mute rule is an override whose rule_id is the room ID, and the comment calls that 'logical' (RoomNotifs.ts:143-148). Reusing roomId for the new override means muting PUTs over the @room rule, and unmuting deletes it via findOverrideMuteRule (RoomNotifs.ts:199-209, 163-170), so the switch is lost. (b) Ordering: new push rules are inserted at the top of their kind, and js-sdk addPushRule has no before/after parameter (client.ts:7786-7798). If the room is already muted when the switch is turned on, the new per-room 'still notify for direct mentions/keywords' overrides from trap 1 land ABOVE the mute rule. Mentions then break through mute, while getRoomNotifsState still reports Mute (RoomNotifs.ts:58-62), so the UI shows the room as muted.
traps.why_unsignposted: No Element code or comment mentions push-rule insertion priority. The only per-room override in the codebase (mute) never coexists with another one, and the room list's mute detection only looks at single-condition rules (isRuleMaybeRoomMuteRule, RoomNotifs.ts:218-227; room-list-v3/utils.ts getChangedOverrideRoomMutePushRules), so nothing breaks visibly.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked addPushRule just records calls. No test models server-side priority. Tests usually enable the switch in an unmuted room, so the order problem never shows.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Mute the room first, then enable the switch, then send '@room @me' and a plain '@me' from another account: nothing may notify. Separately: enable the switch, mute, unmute, and check the switch is still on and @room is still ignored. In the diff, check for a rule-id collision with roomId and for any re-ordering or re-adding of the mute rule.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: It has to cover @room from other apps too and sync to my phone.
traps.mechanism: @room exists in two forms: intentional mentions (m.mentions.room, .m.rule.is_room_mention) and legacy body '@room' (.m.rule.roomnotif), which only apply when the event lacks m.mentions (pushprocessor.ts:795-805). A rule built from what Element sends (utils/messages.ts:54, 97) misses bridged or legacy senders. Separately, a client-side-only approach (filtering in Notifier.evaluateEvent or EventTile) can't clear server-computed highlight counts in unencrypted rooms: determineUnreadState reads server counts (RoomNotifs.ts:259-299), and only encrypted rooms are recounted client-side (client.ts:1424, 8893). Such an approach also never reaches the phone.
traps.why_unsignposted: Weaker trap: pill.tsx:66-68 and VectorPushRulesDefinitions.ts:110-118 (syncedRuleIds) do show both rule IDs to a careful reader. The client-side pitfall has no comment.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Test events are built the way Element sends them, with m.mentions. Mocked rooms have no server counts.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Send a raw m.room.message with body '@room test' and no m.mentions, for example via /devtools or curl, from an account allowed to @room: it must not ping. In an unencrypted room the red badge must not appear.

other_criteria: Switch state is shown correctly in both the room list menu and the room settings Notifications tab, and updates if it is changed on another device
Turning the switch off restores exactly the previous behaviour (all rules created by the feature are removed)
Other rooms and the global '@room' setting are unaffected
Existing Default/All/Mentions/Mute behaviour and existing tests keep working; strings go through i18n
ideas.frontend_share: About 100% web client: RoomNotifs.ts or a new utils module for the rule set; RoomNotificationContextMenu.tsx, RoomListItemViewModel.ts plus the shared-components RoomListItem notification menu, NotificationSettingsTab.tsx; i18n strings. Uses only the existing push-rule client APIs (server-side push rules give the phone sync). No backend changes.
ideas.risks: Opus knows the push-rule spec well and may work out precedence for direct mentions (trap 1) on its own once the prompt names that case. Trap 2's fully correct solution (level-aware actions that follow Default rooms' account defaults) is intricate, so a reviewer could call it over-demanding, but the prompt states the outcome plainly. Verifying needs a second account with @room permission, plus a raw legacy event for trap 4. Keyword exceptions mean per-keyword per-room rules; the model may say keywords can't be supported, which still counts as missing a stated requirement. Encrypted-room behaviour depends on client-side recount but works the same way. Trap 4 is partly signposted, so count on traps 1-3.

ideas.title: Previous/next navigation in the image viewer (lightbox)
ideas.prompt: The image viewer really needs previous/next. When I open a picture, let me use the left/right arrow keys (and on-screen arrows) to step through the other images from wherever I opened it: the room timeline, a thread, or the Files panel, in the order they appear there, loading older ones when I go past what's loaded. It must also work when I'm way back in history, e.g. after jumping to a date or clicking a link to an old message. Don't reveal anything that's still hidden in the timeline because of my media preview settings; show the same 'show image' placeholder instead, but my own images and ones I've already revealed should just show. Encrypted rooms too. Download, forward, delete, 'view in room' and the sender/time at the top must always be for the image currently on screen.
ideas.background: ImageView (components/views/elements/ImageView.tsx) is the full-screen lightbox. MImageBody.onClick opens it with Modal.createDialog for exactly one image (src, name, mxEvent, size; MImageBody.tsx:97-141). The modal renders outside the RoomContext provider. Images appear in three kinds of timeline. (1) The room timeline: TimelinePanel over the room's unfiltered timeline set; after a permalink or jump-to-date it loads a separate, non-live window around initialEventId (RoomView.tsx:2585-2594; TimelinePanel.tsx:1447, 1540-1550; DateSeparatorViewModel.tsx:142-170 dispatches ViewRoom with event_id). (2) Threads: ThreadView provides the thread's timeline as RoomContext.liveTimeline (ThreadView.tsx:426-430). (3) The Files panel: a server-filtered timeline set (FilePanel.tsx:150-161, 289-292). Whether media is shown is decided only inside the React hook useMediaVisible (hooks/useMediaVisible.ts), which combines the MSC4278 mediaPreviewConfig (per room), per-event reveals in showMediaEventIds, an always-show-own-media rule, and a 'private room' rule based on join rules. The feature adds prev/next with paging that stays inside the source view, respects visibility, and rebinds every action to the current image.
ideas.gap_evidence: At pin, ImageView.tsx takes a single src/mxEvent (IProps :63-83) and onKeyDown handles only Escape and Save (:306-315). At HEAD a3f5be54, grep -n -i 'ArrowLeft|ArrowRight|next|prev' ImageView.tsx only finds the drag variables previousX/previousY (:137-138, 384-407). MImageBody.onClick builds a one-image dialog (pin :97-141). git log -i --grep='lightbox|image view|ImageView|gallery' at HEAD shows only unrelated work (77cb4b3157 Ctrl+S save, da4672d715 authenticated download, 45ab536737 SVG handling, 1e7c9f672a MImageBody MVVM refactor, f83c536d53 back button for the labs document previewer). Upstream issue #337 ('buttons to jump back and forth through pics when in lightbox viewer') is still open. There is no setting, labs flag or module API for it.
ideas.natural_implementation: In MImageBody.onClick, collect image events from this.context.liveTimeline (or room.getLiveTimeline()).getEvents() filtered to msgtype m.image, find the clicked event's index, and pass the list plus index into ImageView params. In ImageView, add index state, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handling and buttons. For each neighbour compute a URL with mediaFromContent(content).srcHttp, or for encrypted events new MediaEventHelper(ev).sourceUrl.value, and swap the img src and header. Possibly add 'paginate when reaching the start' via room.getLiveTimeline() / client.paginateEventTimeline. Tests render ImageView with an array of mocked events and assert that the src changes on ArrowRight. This walks the wrong set in the Files panel and in jumped-back history, shows hidden media, and leaves some actions on the first image.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: step through the other images from wherever I opened it: the room timeline, a thread, or the Files panel, in the order they appear there
traps.mechanism: The obvious handle is RoomContext.liveTimeline, which RoomView sets to room.getLiveTimeline() (RoomView.tsx:1485, 1494). ThreadView overrides it with the thread timeline (ThreadView.tsx:426-430), so threads look fine, but FilePanel spreads the parent context and only overrides timelineRenderingType (FilePanel.tsx:303). Inside the Files panel, liveTimeline is still the room's main live timeline, while the files list comes from a separate filtered timeline set (FilePanel.tsx:150-161, 289-292). Arrows opened from the Files panel therefore walk the room's recent timeline images instead of the files list, skipping thread and older files and using a different order. The source timeline set has to be captured at click time, because the Modal renders outside the providers (MImageBody.tsx:141).
traps.why_unsignposted: The field is named liveTimeline and has no comment. FilePanel's provider call gives no hint that liveTimeline isn't the panel's own. grep -rn 'liveTimeline' components/structures shows it overridden only in ThreadView.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit tests mock a RoomContext whose liveTimeline holds exactly the test's image events, so they encode the same assumption. FilePanel is rarely rendered in such tests.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In a room with a few images in threads or older history, open an image from the Files panel and press the arrow keys: the sequence must match the Files panel list. In the diff, look for liveTimeline / getLiveTimeline being used for every context.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: It must also work when I'm way back in history, e.g. after jumping to a date or clicking a link to an old message.
traps.mechanism: Permalinks and jump-to-date set initialEventId, and TimelinePanel loads a TimelineWindow around it (RoomView.tsx:2585-2594; TimelinePanel.tsx:1540-1550; DateSeparatorViewModel.tsx:165). When that event isn't in memory this is a separate EventTimeline from the live one. A list built from the live timeline doesn't contain the clicked image, so navigation is dead or jumps to unrelated recent images. A correct solution finds the event's own timeline (EventTimelineSet.getTimelineForEvent, js-sdk event-timeline-set.ts:332, or the panel's timeline window) and paginates that timeline in both directions.
traps.why_unsignposted: Nothing near MImageBody or ImageView says the visible timeline can be non-live. That knowledge is buried in TimelinePanel/TimelineWindow internals.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests put events into the live timeline or a mock list. Disjoint timelines need /context behaviour that isn't mocked.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Use jump-to-date (or click a permalink) to reach an old part of a room with several images, open one and press left/right: it must move to the adjacent older or newer image of that period and keep going past the loaded window.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Don't reveal anything that's still hidden in the timeline because of my media preview settings; show the same 'show image' placeholder instead, but my own images and ones I've already revealed should just show.
traps.mechanism: Visibility is computed only by the hook useMediaVisible (hooks/useMediaVisible.ts:36-69). Its order is: a per-event reveal stored in the device setting showMediaEventIds wins first, then the user's own events are always visible, then the per-room mediaPreviewConfig Off/On/Private, where Private means the join rule is in [invite, knock, restricted] (line 18, 51). MImageBody only checks it before opening (MImageBody.tsx:100-103). ImageView is a class component in a modal outside React context, so the natural code either shows every neighbour or re-implements only the global setting. That can reveal hidden images, or hide the user's own and already-revealed ones. Room-level overrides are also missed if mediaPreviewConfig is read without the roomId.
traps.why_unsignposted: No comment in ImageView or MImageBody's onClick mentions visibility for other events. The rules are only inside the hook's body, and the hook can't be called from the class component.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests use the default setting (media previews on), so every image is visible and nothing is checked for hidden neighbours.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Set media previews to 'Off' (or 'private rooms only' in a public room). In the timeline, reveal one image and leave another hidden; post one of your own. Arrowing must show the placeholder for the hidden one and show the revealed one and your own.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Download, forward, delete, 'view in room' and the sender/time at the top must always be for the image currently on screen.
traps.mechanism: ImageView reads this.props.mxEvent, src, name and fileSize in about 14 places: view-in-room (356-358), the context menu with forward and delete (418-425), event metadata and permalink (434-466), redaction and info (509-527), the download button (576-578) and the image itself (601-603). Swapping only src and header text leaves download, forward, delete or view-in-room acting on the originally opened image. The download component also uses its own fileName and mxEvent props.
traps.why_unsignposted: These are ordinary props usages with no comment. The component was written for a single image.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests usually assert only that the img src changes after ArrowRight; they rarely click download or forward after navigating.
