ideas.title: Web vault 'Duplicate logins' report with one-click Merge
ideas.prompt: We've got tons of duplicate logins from years of imports. Could you add a 'Duplicate logins' report under Reports in the web vault? Group logins with the same username and the same website (ignore http/https and a leading www.). For each group I pick the one to keep and click Merge. The kept item should end up with all the websites, custom fields and attachments of the others, their notes appended, and whichever password was changed most recently. Every other password in the group, plus each item's old password history, goes into the kept item's password history (newest first; the usual 5-entry limit is fine). For organization items the kept item has to stay in every collection the copies were in. The copies then go to the trash. Only offer Merge when I'm actually allowed to edit the kept item and delete the copies, and never group items from different vaults or organizations.
ideas.background: apps/web has a Reports area (apps/web/src/app/dirt/reports) with vault-health reports (exposed, reused, weak, unsecured websites, inactive 2FA, breach). They all extend CipherReportComponent (pages/cipher-report.component.ts), load ciphers with cipherService.getAllDecrypted, filter them (reused-passwords-report.component.ts:72-80 drops deleted, non-editable and hidden-password items) and show a table that opens the item dialog. Vault items (ciphers) are end-to-end encrypted. An existing item is saved by calling cipherService.encrypt(view, userId, ..., originalCipher) and then cipherService.updateWithServer. Attachments are encrypted files stored on the server under one cipher id. Org items can be in several collections. Delete permission comes from the server as cipher.permissions.delete, so with the org setting 'limit item deletion' an editor may not be allowed to delete. The feature adds a new report that groups duplicate logins and a merge action: it writes the combined data into the kept item and soft-deletes the copies.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin: apps/web/src/app/dirt/reports/pages has only breach, exposed, inactive-two-factor, reused, unsecured-websites and weak reports. Running grep -rli duplicate over apps/web/src/app/dirt, libs/vault/src and libs/common/src/vault finds only a test fixture name in report-utils.spec.ts. grep -rn 'mergeCipher|mergeItems|merge-items' over apps/web/src and libs returns nothing. HEAD 443b03531a (2026-11-04) is the same: the reports dir adds only passkey-report, the browser vault-health risk categories are exposed/weak/reused (libs/common/src/dirt/vault-health/models/risk-category.ts), and the only 'duplicate' hits are a 'deduplicated' doc comment and duplicateAttachmentNameError. git log origin/main -i --grep='duplicate' and --grep='merge item|merge cipher|merge duplicate' show no duplicate-item or merge feature. bitwarden_license has no matching file names at either commit. No setting, labs flag or module covers it.
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Add DuplicateLoginsReportComponent extending CipherReportComponent, copying reused-passwords-report: getAllDecrypted, skip deleted, non-login, !edit and !viewPassword items, then group by (organizationId, username, normalized host of each URI). 2) Add a route in reports-routing.module.ts, a card in reports.ts / reports-home, and i18n strings. 3) Add a merge dialog where the user picks the item to keep. 4) Merge service: pick the newest password using login.passwordRevisionDate falling back to revisionDate; set kept.login.uris to the union, kept.fields to the concatenation, append notes, kept.attachments = [...kept.attachments, ...others.attachments], kept.passwordHistory = sorted union of the other passwords and all histories, kept.collectionIds = union. 5) Call cipherService.encrypt(kept, userId, undefined, undefined, await cipherService.get(kept.id)) and then updateWithServer, or call DefaultCipherFormService.saveCipher. 6) Gate the Merge button on kept.edit && copies.every(c => c.edit), then call cipherService.softDeleteManyWithServer(copyIds). 7) Write Jest tests with mocked CipherService that assert the view passed to encrypt has the merged history and attachments and that softDelete got called.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Every other password in the group, plus each item's old password history, goes into the kept item's password history
traps.mechanism: cipherService.encrypt runs adjustCipherHistory before both the legacy and the SDK encryption paths (libs/common/src/vault/services/cipher.service.ts:262-269). For any view with an id, adjustCipherHistory (cipher.service.ts:250-260) loads the stored original via this.get(model.id) when none is passed and calls updateModelfromExistingCipher, whose first line (cipher.service.ts:1651) is model.passwordHistory = existingCipher.passwordHistory || []. That throws away whatever history the caller put on the view. Lines 1652-1661 then only prepend the kept item's own previous password, and only if it changed. So every password and history entry that came from the copies is silently lost, and passing originalCipher (the pattern used in default-cipher-form.service.ts:72-83) does the same thing. At HEAD it is unchanged: encrypt at cipher.service.ts:311-318 still calls adjustCipherHistory, and line 1532 still has the same assignment. A correct merge has to get around this, for example by building the request so the history survives or by changing the service.
traps.why_unsignposted: The abstraction encrypt(model, userId, keyForEncryption?, keyForCipherKeyDecryption?, originalCipher?) at libs/common/src/vault/abstractions/cipher.service.ts:46-52 has no doc comment. grep -rn passwordHistory over apps/web/src and libs/vault/src (excluding specs) only finds password-history-view.component.ts:26 reading the field, and nothing anywhere sets history on an existing item. cipher.service.spec.ts has no test about history overwrite (its only hit is fixture data at line 83). The only hint is shareWithServer's doc comment (abstractions:132), which is on a different method.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Natural tests mock CipherService.encrypt and updateWithServer and assert that the view passed to encrypt contains the merged history. That passes, because the overwrite happens inside the real encrypt. Only an end-to-end run against a server shows it.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Read the diff. If it sets kept.passwordHistory and then calls cipherService.encrypt or CipherFormService.saveCipher on the existing item with no bypass, the merged history is lost, which cipher.service.ts:1651 confirms. To test by hand: merge A (kept, newest password) with B (different password and one history entry). A's history afterwards does not contain B's password or B's history.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: The kept item should end up with all the ... attachments of the others
traps.mechanism: Attachments are files stored on the server for one cipher. CipherRequest only sends attachment metadata keyed by attachment id (libs/common/src/vault/models/request/cipher.request.ts:196-208). Uploads always go to a specific cipher through saveAttachmentRawWithServer -> cipherFileUploadService.upload(cipher, ...) (cipher.service.ts:1044-1086) and POST /ciphers/{id}/attachment/v2 (api.service.ts:597-601). There is no move endpoint (api.service.ts:574-649). When an item changes owner, the client downloads, decrypts, re-encrypts and re-uploads every attachment (shareAttachmentWithServer, cipher.service.ts:1702-1759). The natural merge copies the AttachmentView objects onto the kept view and saves it. The server never attaches those files to the kept item, its response only lists the kept item's own attachments, and the files disappear when the trashed copies are purged.
traps.why_unsignposted: Nothing near the save path warns that attachment metadata cannot be moved between items: the encrypt, encryptAttachments and updateWithServer signatures look generic. grep for code that copies attachments between ciphers (attachments = / attachments.push in apps/web/src, libs/vault/src and libs/common/src/vault) only finds vault-item-dialog.component.ts:512, which refreshes the same cipher, plus stories. The clone path has no comment about attachments either.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: With CipherService mocked, a test asserting that encrypt received the combined attachments array passes. Nothing checks for download and re-upload calls unless the author already knows they are needed.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Look for download (getAttachmentData + fetch + getDecryptedAttachmentBuffer) and re-upload (saveAttachmentRawWithServer to the kept cipher) of each copy's attachments in the diff. If the attachments array is only concatenated, the requirement fails. By hand: merge an item that has an attachment into one that has none, then reload. The attachment is not on the kept item.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Only offer Merge when I'm actually allowed to edit the kept item and delete the copies
traps.mechanism: Delete rights are separate from edit rights. CipherAuthorizationService.canDeleteCipher$ (libs/common/src/vault/services/cipher-authorization.service.ts:79-94) returns cipher.permissions?.delete, a server-computed flag (models/api/cipher-permissions.api.ts) that reflects the org's limitItemDeletion setting (admin-console/models/domain/organization.ts:82). The code a model copies uses edit instead: the reports filter on edit (reused-passwords-report.component.ts:72-80), and the individual vault's own bulk delete check is ciphers.every((c) => c.edit) (apps/web/src/app/vault/individual-vault/vault.component.ts:1197). Gating on edit shows Merge for org copies the user cannot delete. The server then rejects the soft delete after the kept item has already been rewritten, so the merge is left half done.
traps.why_unsignposted: The nearest patterns (the report filters and vault.component.ts:1197) use edit, with no comment saying deletion differs. canDeleteCipher$ only shows up in vault-items.component.ts:112-113, vault-item-dialog and view.component, which a report author would not normally open.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests build mock CipherViews with edit true or false and assert the button shows or hides. They encode the same edit-means-delete assumption and never set permissions.delete.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Grep the diff for permissions.delete, canDeleteCipher$ or appCanDeleteCipher. If gating only uses edit, it fails. By hand: an org with 'limit item deletion' on and a member with Can edit (not Manage) on a collection that holds duplicates. Merge is offered and then fails part-way.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: and whichever password was changed most recently
traps.mechanism: login.passwordRevisionDate is only set when an existing item's password changes (cipher.service.ts:1653-1663). New items skip adjustCipherHistory because model.id is null (cipher.service.ts:251), so an item whose password was never changed has passwordRevisionDate = null, and the password effectively dates from creationDate. revisionDate (cipher.view.ts:50) moves on any edit, such as a rename or a notes change. The natural choices, passwordRevisionDate ?? revisionDate or treating null as oldest, pick the wrong password: an item created yesterday loses to one whose password changed two years ago, or a renamed item wins with an old password. The repo's own display logic shows the semantics (cipher.view.ts:135-142 passwordRevisionDisplayDate, item-history-v2.component.html:20-26 shows 'Password updated' only when it is set).
traps.why_unsignposted: LoginView.passwordRevisionDate (login.view.ts:22) has no comment, and no code in apps/web or libs/vault orders items by password age. The rule is only visible inside the private updateModelfromExistingCipher.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Test fixtures set passwordRevisionDate on every mock item, or set nothing and rely on revisionDate, so the null-means-never-changed case never comes up.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Read the comparator in the diff. It must fall back to creationDate when passwordRevisionDate is null, not to revisionDate and not to always-oldest. By hand: create B today and leave its password alone, and give A a password change a week ago plus a rename today. B's password must win.

other_criteria: Groups only contain items with the same organizationId (or all personal), the same username and a matching website host after removing the http/https scheme and a leading www.
Copies are soft-deleted (they end up in Trash), not permanently deleted.
Notes from the copies are appended to the kept item's notes, and all websites and custom fields are kept.

For org items the kept item ends up in the union of the copies' collections. This needs saveCollectionsWithServer, because the PUT ignores collectionIds; the comment at libs/vault/src/cipher-form/services/default-cipher-form.service.ts:87 signposts this, so it is graded but not counted as a silent trap.
Hidden-password and deleted items stay out of the report, consistent with the other reports.
The report is linked from Reports home and the merge refreshes the report.
ideas.frontend_share: 100% client. New report component, html and route in apps/web/src/app/dirt/reports (reports-routing.module.ts, reports.ts, reports-home), a merge dialog, a merge service in apps/web or libs/vault, and i18n in apps/web/src/locales/en/messages.json. It uses only existing server endpoints: PUT /ciphers/{id}, PUT /ciphers/{id}/collections_v2, POST /ciphers/{id}/attachment/v2, attachment download, and PUT /ciphers/delete.
ideas.risks: A strong model that opens cipherService.encrypt will see adjustCipherHistory on its first line and may realise the history is overwritten; I estimate about 50% catch it. Many models already know Bitwarden attachments are per-item files and will re-upload them (about 55% catch). The delete-permission trap fails if the model searches for 'canDelete' (about 50%). The collections rule is signposted by a comment, so it is graded only as a criterion. If the model uploads attachments before the PUT, the server may reject the update with 'client copy out of date'; that is server-side behaviour, so it is not graded. Grouping rules for items with several URIs are not graded (possible ambiguity). The feature is large, which adds surface but is not hard on its own.

ideas.title: Import option 'Update existing items' instead of creating duplicates
ideas.prompt: Re-importing exports keeps doubling our vault. On the Import page, add an 'Update existing items' checkbox. When it's ticked, an item in the file that matches one already in the vault I'm importing into (same type and name, plus the same username for logins; items in the trash don't count) should update that item instead of being added again: use the file's password, notes and websites and keep everything else it already has. If the password changed, the old one has to end up in the item's password history, along with any password history the file has for it (Bitwarden .json backups have it). Items without a match import like today and must still land in the folders or collections the file puts them in. If I couldn't change that item's password from the normal edit screen, import the file's version as a new item instead. The success dialog should say how many were added and how many updated.
ideas.background: Imports go through libs/importer: ImportComponent (components/import.component.ts:406-465) calls ImportService.import (services/import.service.ts). There an importer parses the file into an ImportResult (models/import-result.ts) holding ciphers[], folders[] and collections[], plus folderRelationships / collectionRelationships as [cipherIndex, folderIndex] pairs. Those indexes are positions in the ciphers array, recorded at parse time with result.ciphers.length (base-importer.ts:386-388, bitwarden-json-importer.ts:102-114 and 145-156). handleIndividualImport and handleOrganizationalImport (import.service.ts:424-474) encrypt every cipher and send the pairs unchanged as KvpRequest(r[0], r[1]) to the bulk import endpoint. Bitwarden JSON backups carry per-item passwordHistory (bitwarden-json-importer.ts:96-99 and 139-142). ImportSuccessDialogComponent counts result.ciphers by type. The feature: match imported items against existing vault items, update matches in place and import the rest.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin: grep -rn -i 'existing|overwrite|updateExisting|skip' over libs/importer/src/services/import.service.ts and components/import.component.ts finds nothing. HEAD 443b03531a: the same grep only finds unrelated hits, namely 'preserve any existing folders' for DefaultUserCollection targets (import.service.ts:704) and ImportSkippedItemsDialog / onePasswordPartialImport, which are about parse errors, not duplicates. git log origin/main -i -E --grep='re-?import|existing item|skip duplicate|update existing|overwrite existing' has no relevant commit. No importer option, setting or flag avoids duplicates; re-importing always creates new ciphers because the Bitwarden JSON importer resets cipher.id = null (bitwarden-json-importer.ts:91-93 and 134-136).
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Add an updateExisting form control to ImportComponent and pass it into importService.import. 2) In ImportService.import, after parsing and next to the restricted-type filter at import.service.ts:228-231: load cipherService.getAllDecrypted(userId), keep the target vault's items (organizationId === orgId or null) that are not deleted, and build a match map by type, name and username. 3) For each imported cipher with a match where existing.edit is true: set existing.login.password, notes and uris from the file, set existing.passwordHistory = [...imported.passwordHistory, ...existing.passwordHistory], then cipherService.encrypt(existing, userId) and updateWithServer. 4) Drop the matched ciphers with importResult.ciphers = importResult.ciphers.filter(c => !matched.has(c)), copying the restricted-type filter, and continue with setImportTarget and handleIndividualImport or handleOrganizationalImport. 5) Add updatedCount to ImportResult and show it in ImportSuccessDialogComponent. 6) Write Jest tests with mocked importer, CipherService and ImportApiService that check updateWithServer calls and the request.ciphers length.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Items without a match import like today and must still land in the folders or collections the file puts them in
traps.mechanism: folderRelationships and collectionRelationships hold positions in importResult.ciphers, recorded during parsing (base-importer.ts:386-388; bitwarden-json-importer.ts:102-114 and 145-156), and handleIndividualImport / handleOrganizationalImport send them unchanged (import.service.ts:440-443 and 468-471). Removing matched ciphers from importResult.ciphers, or skipping them when building request.ciphers, shifts every later cipher's index. The pairs then point at the wrong cipher or past the end, so imported items land in other folders or collections, or in none. The neighbouring restricted-type filter (import.service.ts:228-231, still at HEAD import.service.ts:191-194) does exactly this without remapping, so the precedent the model copies is the wrong pattern. The collection-count check at import.service.ts:233-238 also compares lengths and goes stale.
traps.why_unsignposted: There is no comment on the ciphers or relationship fields of ImportResult (models/import-result.ts) saying the indexes are positional. The comment on the filter right next to where the new logic goes ('Filter out restricted item types from the import result') presents a plain filter as safe. The only relationship tests (import.service.spec.ts:243-268) cover setImportTarget's folder-index shift, not removing ciphers.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Natural tests assert which ciphers reach postImportCiphers and that updateWithServer was called for matches. A test with folder relationships only catches the bug if the author already reasons about indexes; one that checks only that folders were sent passes.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Read the diff. If ciphers are filtered or skipped without rebuilding folderRelationships and collectionRelationships, it fails. By hand: a CSV or JSON file where item 1 matches an existing item and item 2 is in folder 'Work'. After import, item 2 is not in 'Work'.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: the old one has to end up in the item's password history, along with any password history the file has for it
traps.mechanism: Any update of an existing item goes through cipherService.encrypt, which first calls adjustCipherHistory (cipher.service.ts:262-269, 250-260). That replaces the view's history with the stored one (cipher.service.ts:1651: model.passwordHistory = existingCipher.passwordHistory || []) and then prepends only the item's previous password (1653-1661). Whether the model merges the file's history into the existing view or saves the imported view with the existing id, the file's history is dropped. The automatic 'old password into history' part works, so a quick manual check looks right. HEAD is unchanged (cipher.service.ts:311-318 and 1532).
traps.why_unsignposted: encrypt has no doc comment (abstractions/cipher.service.ts:46-52). The import path only ever calls encrypt on new ciphers (id null), where adjustCipherHistory does nothing (cipher.service.ts:251), so nothing in libs/importer hints that history behaves differently on update. No test in cipher.service.spec.ts covers it.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: CipherService is mocked in import.service.spec.ts (it uses mock<CipherService>()), so a test asserting that encrypt received the combined history passes.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Check whether the diff sets passwordHistory and then calls encrypt on an item with an existing id without working around adjustCipherHistory. By hand: re-import a Bitwarden .json whose item has 2 history entries and a new password. The updated item shows only its own old password, not the file's entries.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: If I couldn't change that item's password from the normal edit screen, import the file's version as a new item instead
traps.mechanism: The edit screen disables password and TOTP when the user may edit but not view passwords ('Can edit, except passwords'): login-details-section.component.ts:99-103, 160-162 and 179-181 gate on originalCipherView.viewPassword. The domain helper cipher.view.ts:162-169 uses edit && viewPassword for org items. The natural check is cipher.edit, as in the report filters and vault.component.ts:1197, so it overwrites the password of an item whose password the user is not even allowed to see.
traps.why_unsignposted: The import code never looks at permissions. The common permission check in apps/web is cipher.edit, and viewPassword only shows up in view and form components that the import feature does not touch.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests mock existing ciphers with edit true or false only. viewPassword defaults to true on CipherView (cipher.view.ts:39), so the case never shows up.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Grep the update guard in the diff for viewPassword. By hand: an org collection with 'Can edit, except passwords', then import a file matching an item in it. The item must not be changed and a new copy must be created.

other_criteria: Matching only considers the vault being imported into (personal items for My vault, that org's items for an org import) and ignores trashed items.

Matched items keep their folder, favorite, attachments, passkeys, TOTP and custom fields, and only password, notes and URIs come from the file. Note: saving the imported view under the existing id without passing originalCipher makes encrypt mint a new cipher key (cipher.service.ts:295-298, 2016-2018), which breaks existing attachments when they are not copied over. This is a possible extra failure, not a counted trap.
The success dialog shows separate added and updated counts.
When the checkbox is off, behaviour is unchanged.
ideas.frontend_share: 100% client: libs/importer (import.component.ts and html, import.service.ts, ImportResult model, import-success-dialog), web i18n, and possibly the CLI caller of ImportService.import. It uses only existing endpoints: POST /ciphers/import, POST /ciphers/import-organization and PUT /ciphers/{id}.
ideas.risks: A model that reads ImportResult and the setImportTarget index juggling may realise the relationships are positional (I estimate about 55% catch). It may also write a folder-relationship test that exposes the bug. The S1 trap is the same mechanism as idea 1, so the two ideas are not independent. 'Vault I'm importing into' is ambiguous for Admin Console org imports by an admin who is not in every collection, so a reviewer should not grade comparison against unassigned items. Only two strong traps; the third depends on whether the model thinks about hidden-password permissions.

rejected_ideas: Create a Send from a vault item: already exists at HEAD (libs/tools/share with ShareLinkService and the item-send-drawer).
Export organization members to CSV: already exists at HEAD (members/services/member-export).

Org vault .zip export with attachments (missing at pin and HEAD: org-vault-export.service.ts:108-110 throws). The only solid trap is the admin attachment endpoint, and that is signposted in download-attachment.component.ts:37-38. The local-state lookup in getDecryptedAttachmentBuffer only breaks when the SDK flag is on (default FALSE at pin), so it cannot be graded reliably.
Import 'skip duplicates' (instead of update): has only the relationship-index trap plus an org-scope rule a stated prompt points straight at; folded into idea 2.

Delete or restore password history entries: missing at pin and HEAD and hit by the same encrypt overwrite, but small with no second silent trap. Restoring hidden-field history entries would force the model to read updateModelfromExistingCipher and expose the main trap.

Admin Console bulk 'clear password history': the overwrite only hits items in the admin's local state, and the admin-endpoint/partial-update fallback is signposted by admin-console-cipher-form-config.service.ts:121-124, so it is effectively one trap.
Cascade a collection rename to its sub-collections: the dialog already uses collectionAdminViews$ with access details, so the natural path keeps access and there is no silent trap.
Cascade a folder rename or move to its subfolders: just prefix matching and the 'No folder' pseudo entry, which strong models handle.
Authenticator page listing all TOTP codes: premium/useTotp, reprompt and per-item period rules are all visible in vault-cipher-row and TotpService.
Expiring cards report: isCardExpired already exists and RestrictedItemTypesService is easy to find and reuse.
Old passwords (password age) report: only the passwordRevisionDate fallback is a trap; the rest copies the report template.
Clone a Send: new key, password-hash, file re-upload and date limits are obvious once considered and mostly enforced by the server.
Bulk favorite or move: updateWithServer silently falls back to the partial endpoint for read-only items, which happens to be correct for favorite and folder.
Effective collection access overview combining group and direct grants: the combination rule lives on the server, so it cannot be determined from the client repo.

ideas.title: Use the profile time zone (not the browser's) for every time the web app shows or lets you pick
ideas.prompt: A lot of our team travels, so the computer's clock often isn't the time zone people actually work in. Zulip already has a Time zone field in my profile settings, but the web app only uses it to show my local time to other people. Everything I see follows the browser's time zone. Can you make the web app use my profile time zone instead, falling back to the browser's if I haven't set one? That covers message times and the Today/Yesterday date headers, scheduled messages and reminders (including which quick 'send later' options get offered and what time they actually mean), the custom date/time picker, and inserting a global time into a message. Changing the setting should take effect right away, without a reload. Anything that's only a calendar date with no time, like a date field on someone's profile, has to keep showing exactly the date that was entered.
ideas.background: Every Zulip user has a server-side `timezone` setting (Settings > Profile > Time zone, stored in user_settings.timezone). Today the web app uses it only to show your local time to other people. All times in the UI are rendered in the browser's time zone. Display formatting is centralised in web/src/timerender.ts, which keeps a module-level `display_time_zone`/`display_tz` (an @date-fns/tz zone) and a test-only `set_display_time_zone()`. Several other features compute wall-clock times on their own with plain JS `Date` methods. These are the 'send later'/'remind me' quick options ('Today at 9:00 AM', 'Tomorrow at 4:00 PM', 'Monday at 9:00 AM'), the flatpickr date/time picker used for custom scheduling, reminders and global-time insertion (`<time:...>`), and the display of DATE-type custom profile fields. The feature makes the profile zone the effective zone for both showing and picking times, updates live when the setting changes, and must not shift date-only values.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin: `grep -rn "set_display_time_zone(\|user_settings.timezone" web/src` hits only timerender.ts:37 (definition), timerender.ts:342/346 (initialize() falls back to user_settings.timezone ONLY when the browser zone is undefined or 'Etc/Unknown'), navbar_alerts.ts:177 (the 'your computer's time zone differs' banner) and settings_account.ts:332/338 (the dropdown). timerender.ts:23 `export let display_time_zone = browser_time_zone();`. Upstream HEAD (1f9b9109b5, Nov 2026) is the same: head/web/src/timerender.ts:23 is still browser_time_zone(), set_display_time_zone is called only in the initialize fallback (head timerender.ts:364/368), and head scheduled_messages.ts:41-55 still uses setHours. `git log --grep` finds only a2c6c11296 'timerender: Track browser time zone', b6d8bf3a80 'navbar_alerts: Add alert to update time zone' and the web_suggest_update_timezone setting. None of these does it. GitHub issue #16958 'Display settings → Time zone is not used for display' is open. No setting or labs flag covers it.
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) In timerender.initialize() (which already reads user_settings.timezone as a fallback) call `set_display_time_zone(user_settings.timezone || browser_time_zone())`, keeping the invalid-zone try/catch. 2) In server_events_dispatch.js, where user_settings updates for 'timezone' arrive (the property is already listed at line 932), call set_display_time_zone and rerender the message lists, copying the twenty_four_hour_time handler at lines 975-982. 3) Because every display helper in timerender uses display_tz/display_time_zone, conclude that timestamps, date headers, tooltips, scheduled/reminder lists and drafts are all handled. 4) Possibly patch flatpickr's output. 5) Add node tests that call set_display_time_zone('Asia/Kolkata') around timerender.render_now and similar helpers. The test runner forces TZ=UTC, so these pass.

ideas.title: Silence desktop pop-ups and sounds for mentions of chosen user groups
ideas.prompt: I'm in a lot of user groups, and pings to groups like @support or @oncall bury the stuff that's actually for me. Can you add a section to Notifications settings where I choose which of my groups' @-mentions shouldn't trigger a desktop pop-up or sound? Remembering it in this browser is fine. A message that pings a silenced group should be treated like any other message in that conversation. If that channel is set to notify me about every message, or it's a followed topic I get notified for, I still get it; in a muted topic I get nothing. But if the same message also @-mentions me by name, pings another group I'm in that I haven't silenced, or uses @all/@topic and I normally get those, notify me like today. Mentions that only appear inside a quoted message shouldn't count.
ideas.background: In the Zulip web app, desktop pop-ups and sounds are decided client-side in web/src/message_notifications.ts. message_is_notifiable() checks muting and lets 'direct mentions' override it. should_send_desktop_notification() and should_send_audible_notification() check per-channel 'all messages' settings, followed-topic settings, the global DM/mention switches, and then the wildcard-mention settings. Messages carry booleans derived from server flags in message_store.ts: `mentioned` and `mentioned_me_directly`. User-group mentions render in content as `<span class="user-group-mention" data-user-group-id=..>`, personal mentions as `.user-mention[data-user-id]`, and silent mentions (including all mentions inside quotes, which the server silences) carry `.silent`. The feature adds a per-browser list of silenced groups and makes a ping that reaches you only through silenced groups behave like a mention-free message.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin and HEAD: `grep -in group web/src/message_notifications.ts` hits only line 137/135 (a comment about group DMs). web/templates/settings/notification_settings.hbs has no user-group options at pin or HEAD (the 'group' hits are only CSS 'input-group'). `git log --oneline -iE --grep="mute.*group|silence.*group|group.*notification" origin/main -- web/src` finds only an unrelated recent-conversations commit. Server-side there's no per-group notification setting either. Users can only turn off wildcard mentions (wildcard_mentions_notify) or mute channels/topics.
ideas.natural_implementation: Add a pill or checkbox list of `user_groups.get_user_groups_of_user(my_id)` to Settings > Notifications, stored in localStorage. In message_notifications, add `is_only_silenced_group_mention(message)`. It parses message.content for `.user-group-mention` ids in the silenced set and treats `message.mentioned_me_directly` as 'personal @-mention'. It is used to skip the `if (message.mentioned_me_directly) return true` early-outs in message_is_notifiable (line 248) and in should_send_desktop/audible_notification (lines 321, 393), or to return false early in received_messages. Unit tests mock messages with `mentioned_me_directly: false` plus group-mention HTML for 'group-only' pings, matching the existing test vocabulary.

The `group_mentioned` flag exists in zerver/models/messages.py:480 but is never set when sending. The web maps that flag to `mentioned_me_directly: convert_flag("mentioned")` (message_store.ts:303, and update_booleans at 364). So every silenced-group ping has mentioned_me_directly === true. Code that uses that field to mean 'mentioned me by name' never suppresses anything, and pings in muted topics still notify through the line-248 override.

Note that @all mentions are still suppressed by muting.' web/tests/notifications.test.cjs:221-223 describes `mentioned_me_directly: false` as 'does not mention the user DIRECTLY (i.e. wildcard mention)'. Group mentions appear nowhere on this path. Diff: personal mention must be detected from content (`.user-mention[data-user-id=me]:not(.silent)`, as message_list_view.ts:634 does), not from mentioned_me_directly.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Mentions that only appear inside a quoted message shouldn't count.
traps.mechanism: The server rewrites mentions inside blockquotes to silent mentions (zerver/lib/markdown/__init__.py:1555-1559; client mirror markdown.ts:338-367), so they render with class `silent` and set no flag. A content-based check written as `.user-mention[data-user-id="me"]` or `.user-group-mention[data-user-group-id]` without `:not(.silent)` treats a quoted '@**me**' as a personal mention and notifies for a silenced-group ping. traps.how_reviewer_checks: Quote an earlier message that @-mentioned the user, add '@*support*' (silenced) below it, and send: there must be no notification.

other_criteria: Settings list shows only groups the user belongs to, including via subgroups, and excludes system and deactivated groups
Choice persists across reloads in that browser and applies to the next incoming message without reload
Pings to an unsilenced group I'm in still notify, and a mention of a group I'm not in doesn't create a notification reason
Desktop pop-ups and sounds both respect the setting
Existing notification tests keep passing
ideas.frontend_share: 100% web: message_notifications.ts, settings_notifications.ts plus templates/settings/notification_settings.hbs, a small localStorage helper, web/tests. No backend change.
ideas.risks: If the model greps 'group mention' it hits message_list_view.ts:629, which explains the flag conflation, and Opus may also recall from the API docs that `mentioned` includes group mentions. Rewriting the decision as 'compute effective flags, then run the normal logic' handles traps 2 and 3 together. Storing per browser is a slightly unusual product choice for Zulip, but the prompt asks for it explicitly. Grading needs two accounts and a group, which is a short manual setup.

ideas.title: Sync web drafts with the server drafts API (pending web implementation)
ideas.prompt: Our mobile app syncs drafts through the server, but the web app still keeps drafts only in the browser. Can you make web drafts sync with the server's drafts API, so a draft I start on my laptop shows up on my phone and vice versa, including edits and deletions? Once I send a message, its draft shouldn't stick around on my other devices. If I delete a draft on my phone while the laptop is closed, it must not come back when I open Zulip again. If a topic I've got a draft for is renamed or moved, the synced draft should follow it. Please also add the 'Synchronize drafts' toggle to settings: when it's off, drafts stay local like today, and turning it back on should upload whatever drafts are on this computer.
ideas.background: Zulip's server has a full drafts API: GET/POST /drafts, PATCH/DELETE /drafts/{id}, `drafts` events, `drafts` in the register state, and a user setting enable_drafts_synchronization. The API docs mark it x-pending-web-implementation. The web app stores drafts only in localStorage through drafts.ts draft_model, keyed by random local ids. Compose saves drafts via update_draft(), the send flow saves an is_sending_saving draft and deletes it on success, and topic/channel moves rewrite stored drafts via rename_stream_recipient(). The feature wires the two stores together, adds the settings toggle and keeps both sides consistent across devices.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin and HEAD: `grep -rn "json/drafts" web/src` returns nothing. state_data.ts has no drafts schema. server_events_dispatch.js has no 'drafts' case. enable_drafts_synchronization appears only in the zod schemas user_settings.ts:52 and realm_user_settings_defaults.ts:22, with no UI. Upstream commit 83cdbfd28c 'api-docs: Note API feature endpoints without frontend implementation' tags /drafts as x-pending-web-implementation (HEAD zulip.yaml ~7450-7654). `git log --grep=draft` since the pin shows only local-draft UX changes (autosave, arrow navigation), no server sync. The web register (zerver/lib/home.py:109-121) already includes `drafts` in state (zerver/lib/events.py:322-334).
ideas.natural_implementation: Parse state_data.drafts at startup and merge them into draft_model: add server drafts not present locally, and POST local drafts not present on the server. Store server_id on each local draft. Hook draft_model.addDraft/editDraft/deleteDrafts or drafts.update_draft to POST/PATCH/DELETE when user_settings.enable_drafts_synchronization is on. Handle drafts add/update/remove events by writing into draft_model. Convert local {type, stream_id, topic, private_message_recipient_ids, updatedAt} to server {type, to, topic, content, timestamp}. Add a checkbox in Preferences calling the settings API.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: If I delete a draft on my phone while the laptop is closed, it must not come back when I open Zulip again.
traps.mechanism: The obvious startup merge (union: upload local drafts the server doesn't have) can't tell 'deleted elsewhere while I was offline' from 'never synced', because local drafts (drafts.ts:39-62 schema) carry no sync identity. Even with a server_id, the register response holds only the newest MAX_DRAFTS_IN_REGISTER_RESPONSE=1000 drafts (zerver/lib/events.py:322-334, zproject/default_settings.py:679), so 'absent from state' doesn't strictly mean deleted. The naive merge re-POSTs the draft the user deleted, and it reappears on every device.
traps.why_unsignposted: Nothing in drafts.ts or the API docs discusses reconciling after offline deletions. Remove events are sent only to clients connected at the time (zerver/lib/drafts.py do_delete_draft).
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Model tests mock channel.post/patch/del and a state_data.drafts array. A 'union' merge passes a test written with the same assumption.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Create a draft on web (synced), close the tab, DELETE it via the API or mobile, reopen web: the draft must be absent locally and on GET /drafts.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: If a topic I've got a draft for is renamed or moved, the synced draft should follow it.
traps.mechanism: Moves don't go through compose. message_events.ts:606 calls drafts.rename_stream_recipient(), which rewrites drafts with draft_model.editDraft directly (drafts.ts:290-317). If sync is wired into update_draft()/compose (drafts.ts:425-482, where drafts are 'saved'), the server copy keeps the old channel and topic, and the phone and any freshly loaded client show the stale recipient. The server itself never rewrites Draft rows on message moves.
traps.why_unsignposted: rename_stream_recipient has no comment about server state. The compose-side update_draft looks like the single save point.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Sync tests drive update_draft and compose flows. Move handling is tested separately in drafts tests that don't mock the network.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Have a synced draft in topic A, rename topic A to B from another client, then GET /drafts: the topic must be B.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: turning it back on should upload whatever drafts are on this computer
traps.mechanism: When a user turns enable_drafts_synchronization off, the server deletes all their Draft rows without sending remove events (zerver/actions/user_settings.py:604-609). Local drafts keep stale server ids. On re-enable, 'upload drafts without a server id' skips all of them, and later edits PATCH /drafts/{id} and get 'Draft does not exist' (zerver/lib/drafts.py do_edit_draft). Only the server-side comment documents this silent mass deletion.
traps.why_unsignposted: No web code or API event signals the deletion. The draft_endpoint error 'User has disabled synchronizing drafts.' (zerver/lib/drafts.py:89-98) covers the off state, not the off-then-on transition.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked servers in tests don't model the silent deletion. Re-enable tests see the drafts 'already synced'.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Sync a draft, toggle the setting off and on, then GET /drafts: the draft must be on the server again, and editing it must succeed without 404s.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Once I send a message, its draft shouldn't stick around on my other devices.
traps.mechanism: compose.ts:187-197 saves an is_sending_saving draft immediately before transmit, and compose.ts:153 deletes it on success. Hooking sync into draft_model means a POST /drafts for every sent message. If the local delete fires before the POST's id comes back (especially with debounced or queued sync), the DELETE has no id and the server draft is orphaned, so the phone shows a draft of an already-sent message. Units also differ: server `timestamp` is integer seconds (zerver/models/drafts.py:27-36) while local updatedAt is ms (drafts.ts:33-35). Copying one into the other yields 1970 dates or a server 'year out of range' failure in timestamp_to_datetime (zerver/lib/drafts.py:47-53).
traps.why_unsignposted: Nothing near compose.ts:187 says the sending-saving draft is transient from a sync perspective. is_sending_saving is documented only as a reload-recovery flag (drafts.ts:722-733).
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Synchronous mocks resolve POST before the send success callback, so the orphan race never happens in tests.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Send several messages quickly with sync on, then GET /drafts: there must be no leftovers. Check the drafts overlay timestamps for drafts created via the API.

other_criteria: Drafts created on other clients appear in the web Drafts overlay with correct recipient, topic and time
Edits and deletions propagate live through drafts events
With sync off, no /drafts API calls are made and local drafts behave as before
Settings toggle reflects and updates enable_drafts_synchronization, including live updates from other clients
No duplicate drafts in the originating tab when its own add event arrives

ideas.title: Live counts for Starred / Archived / Trash / Untagged and custom smart views that match the list exactly
ideas.prompt: The sidebar shows a count next to Notes, Files and every tag, but Starred, Archived, Trash, Untagged and my own smart views show nothing. Can you add counts there too? The one thing I care about: each number has to match exactly how many items I'd see in that list if I clicked the view right now. That means using the view's own display settings (show archived, show trashed, hide protected, hide pinned, whether set just for that view or globally), and only counting what's visible given the vaults I've hidden or am viewing exclusively. If a smart view shows files as well as notes, count those too, since they're in the list. And keep the numbers live: starring, archiving, trashing, tagging or editing something, changing a view's display settings, or switching vaults should update them right away.
ideas.background: Standard Notes web client (React + MobX over snjs). The sidebar (Components/Tags/SmartViewsListItem.tsx) lists system smart views (Notes, Files, Starred, Archived, Trash, Untagged, Conflicts) and user smart views (saved predicate filters). Tags have live counts (TagsCountsState via ItemCounter). Smart views have a count only for Notes, Files and Conflicts. A view's list is built in layers. ItemListController.reloadDisplayPreferences merges per-view prefs (PrefKey.SystemViewPreferences for system views, item.preferences for custom views) with the global prefs. reloadNotesDisplayOptions builds the criteria. ItemManager.setPrimaryItemDisplayOptions applies per-view overrides, rebuilds the system smart views from the current options, and feeds navigationDisplayController, which also holds the vault visibility options. The feature adds a badge to each remaining view that equals that list's length and stays live.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin f64d5a4a equals origin/main HEAD (2026-11-02), so pin and upstream are the same. SmartViewsListItem.tsx:163-166 renders a count only for SystemViewId.AllNotes, Files and Conflicts. ItemManager.countableNotesForTag throws 'countableItemsForTag is not meant to be used for smart views.' (ItemManager.ts:349-357). TagsCountsState.ts counts tags only. git log -i --grep 'smart view.*count|count.*smart view|view count' finds only the unrelated 'system smart tags on empty account' commits. grep -i count in PrefKey.ts finds no setting or labs flag for view counts.
ideas.natural_implementation: (1) In SmartViewsListItem, for each remaining view, show application.items.notesMatchingSmartView(view).length (exposed on ItemManagerInterface; it sits right below the throwing countableNotesForTag and ItemManager.spec.ts:528 and :609-613 use it as the way to 'use a smart view'). For Trash, reuse notesController.trashedNotesCount, which already drives the 'N notes in Trash' label (NotesOptions.tsx:151,365). (2) A more careful version copies the prefs merge from ItemListController.reloadDisplayPreferences and calls notesAndFilesMatchingOptions({views:[view], includeArchived, includeTrashed, includePinned, includeProtected}, notes, collection), using the view object from navigationController.smartViews. (3) For live updates, hook items.addNoteCountChangeObserver as NavigationController does for the Notes/Files counts (NavigationController.ts:176-187), or streamItems(Note) as the Conflicts count does (SmartViewsListItem.tsx:105-113).

traps.requirement_in_prompt: each number has to match exactly how many items I'd see in that list if I clicked the view right now. That means using the view's own display settings
traps.mechanism: System smart views are cached objects whose predicates are built from the options of whatever view is currently open. setPrimaryItemDisplayOptions calls rebuildSystemSmartViews({...options, ...override}) (ItemManager.ts:139,165,55-58). BuildSmartViews bakes includeTrashed, includeArchived, includeProtected and includePinned into each system predicate (SmartViewBuilder.ts:104,163-218). getSmartViews(), trashSmartView, findItem(SystemViewId) and notesMatchingSmartView all use these cached objects (ItemManager.ts:817-855), and so does navigationController.smartViews (NavigationController.ts:216-226). computeFiltersForDisplayOptions ignores an include option whenever the predicate already mentions that keypath (DisplayOptionsToFilters.ts:68-80), so the clause baked in for another view wins over the target view's own setting. Example: with Notes open, the cached Trash predicate has archived=false, but opening Trash forces includeArchived=true (ItemManager.ts:156-160), so archived-and-trashed notes are in the list but not in the count. Example: open a tag set to 'hide protected' and the Starred count loses protected starred notes, while the Starred list (using its own settings) still shows them.
traps.why_unsignposted: notesMatchingSmartView (ItemManager.ts:817) and BuildSmartViews have no doc comment. rebuildSystemSmartViews is private and appears only inside ItemManager. grep TODO|FIXME in ItemManager.ts, SmartViewBuilder.ts, ItemCounter.ts and SmartViewsListItem.tsx finds nothing. The existing specs present notesMatchingSmartView as the right API.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: A fresh ItemManager in a unit test builds system views with {} (ItemManager.ts:50) and never selects another view first, so the cached predicates look neutral and every count assertion passes. Web-side tests mock items.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In the diff, check whether the count uses view.predicate from cached system views or notesMatchingSmartView, instead of rebuilding that view's predicate from its own options. Manually: archive a note, then trash it. With Notes open, read the Trash count, then click Trash and see one more item in the list. Or set a tag to hide protected, open it, and compare the Starred count with the Starred list.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: using the view's own display settings (show archived, show trashed, hide protected, hide pinned, whether set just for that view or globally)
traps.mechanism: notesMatchingSmartView passes only {views:[view]} (ItemManager.ts:817-827), so no includeArchived, includeTrashed, includeProtected or includePinned filter is ever added (DisplayOptionsToFilters.ts:68-80). The list always passes booleans from prefs (ItemListController.ts:636-677, 714-733). With default settings, the Starred predicate has no 'archived' clause (SmartViewBuilder.ts:201-218), so archived starred notes are counted but hidden in the list. The Untagged predicate has no 'trashed' clause (SmartViewBuilder.ts:182-199), so trashed untagged notes are counted but hidden. The existing Trash label count goes through the same path: trashedItems uses notesMatchingSmartView (ItemManager.ts:845-847; NotesController.ts:252-254).
traps.why_unsignposted: The method name promises the view's matching notes, and the existing 'N notes in Trash' UI uses it. Nothing notes that list semantics differ.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Model-written tests create notes that are neither archived nor trashed, or assert against the same helper, so they encode the same assumption. The existing ItemManager.spec untagged test uses this method.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: With default settings, star a note and archive it: the Starred count includes it and the Starred list does not. Trash an untagged note: the Untagged count includes it and the list does not.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: only counting what's visible given the vaults I've hidden or am viewing exclusively
traps.mechanism: Vault visibility is applied only inside the display controllers and ItemCounter, through setVaultDisplayOptions with ExcludeVaults or ExclusiveVault validators (ItemManager.ts:226-233; ItemCounter.ts:77-102). notesAndFilesMatchingOptions and notesMatchingSmartView know nothing about vaults and iterate every decrypted note (ItemManager.ts:822-826; SearchUtilities.ts:16-26). The list also skips a few ItemManager-only adjustments, such as the Conflicts extra filter (ItemManager.ts:161-163).
traps.why_unsignposted: computeFiltersForDisplayOptions looks like the complete list filter. The vault filter lives in a different class (ItemDisplayController/ItemCounter), with no comment linking them.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit tests do not set vault display options, so all notes are visible.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: With Labs vaults on, hide a vault (or view another vault exclusively): the counts still include starred, archived or trashed notes from the hidden vault, while the lists do not.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: If a smart view shows files as well as notes, count those too ... keep the numbers live: starring, archiving, trashing, tagging or editing something, changing a view's display settings, or switching vaults should update them right away
traps.mechanism: The list's display controller covers Note and File (ItemManager.ts:67-75), but notesMatchingSmartView iterates notes only (ItemManager.ts:824), so a custom view such as one filtering on userModifiedDate undercounts files. For live updates, the obvious hook addNoteCountChangeObserver fires only when an item's countable state or a tag's member set changes size (ItemCounter.ts:104-110,128,163,169). Starring, unstarring, pinning or protecting a note never fires it. Display-pref changes (PrefKey.SystemViewPreferences or tag.preferences) and VaultDisplayOptionsChanged are not item changes at all, so the streamItems precedent misses them too.
traps.why_unsignposted: NavigationController wires the existing counts through addNoteCountChangeObserver with no comment about which changes it reports.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests compute counts once. Nothing re-renders the sidebar after a star or a pref change.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Star a note while looking at Notes: the Starred badge does not change until something unrelated triggers a refresh. Toggle 'show archived' for Starred: the badge stays stale. A custom view that matches files shows fewer items than its list.

other_criteria: Badges render for Starred, Archived, Trash, Untagged and every custom smart view, styled like the tag counts
Custom smart views with tag predicates (tags includes ...) are counted correctly, which needs the ItemWithTags wrapping in DisplayOptionsToFilters.ts:37-46
Conflicted copies are excluded the same way as in the list
Counts do not depend on the current search text
No regression to the existing Notes, Files and Conflicts counts
ideas.frontend_share: About 100% client-side. packages/web: SmartViewsListItem.tsx and NavigationController, or a new SmartViewCountsState. A clean fix may add a pure 'items for view' helper in packages/models or snjs ItemManager and expose it on packages/services ItemManagerInterface. No server or API change.
ideas.risks: Counts already exist for Notes, Files and Conflicts, so a reviewer may see this as extending an existing feature. A very strong model that refactors setPrimaryItemDisplayOptions into a reusable pure function would fix traps 1 and 2 together, since they are correlated. The vault part needs the Labs vaults feature enabled to test by hand. The UI work is small, so the difficulty rests entirely on the hidden semantics. An integration test comparing each count with getDisplayableNotesAndFiles() after selecting that view would expose traps 1-3.

ideas.title: Find and replace across all notes
ideas.prompt: Renaming a client or project means fixing it note by note, which is painful. Can you add a find & replace across all my notes? I type what to find and the replacement, see which notes match and how many hits each has, then replace all in one go. It has to work in plain text, Markdown and Super notes; in Super only the words change, and formatting, images and links stay exactly as they were. Skip trashed notes and notes that use other editors (spreadsheets, authenticator and so on). Skip anything I'm not allowed to edit and tell me what got skipped. Protected notes stay out of the results until I unlock them, like normal search. After it runs, every match should really be replaced, including in the note I have open right now, and the notes list should show the updated text.
ideas.background: Standard Notes has in-note find/replace (UniversalSearch for plain notes, SearchPlugin for Super) and a list search that only filters. There is no way to replace text across notes. Note text lives in SNNote.text: plain or Markdown strings, or Lexical JSON for Super. List previews are separate denormalized fields (preview_plain and preview_html) that the editors write when they save. The open note is shown by NoteView with PlainEditor or SuperEditor, each keeping its own local editor state fed by NoteViewController observers. The feature adds a modal that searches eligible notes, shows hits per note, and rewrites matches in bulk, then syncs.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin equals upstream HEAD (origin/main f64d5a4a). git log -i --grep replace shows only in-note work (810452265 Super search and replace, 1ea8da600 in-note search for plain notes, 386d73ffb). grep -rli 'replace all|replaceAll' in packages/web/src matches only NoteView/UniversalSearch, PlainEditor and SuperEditor SearchPlugin (single note). SearchBar and SearchOptions only filter. No remote branch name mentions replace.
ideas.natural_implementation: (1) A modal opened from the command palette or search options, with find and replace inputs, a case option and a results list. (2) Candidates come from items.getItems(Note), filtered to not trashed and not locked. Protected notes go through protections.authorizeProtectedActionForItems or follow searchOptionsController.includeProtectedContents. (3) Notes are classified by note.noteType. Super text is parsed as JSON, text nodes are walked and the result is re-serialized. Other text uses string replace. (4) Changes are written with mutator.changeItems or changeAndSaveItem.execute(note, m => m.text = newText), sometimes also setting preview_plain to the first 160 chars the way NoteSyncController does, then sync.sync().

traps.requirement_in_prompt: every match should really be replaced, including in the note I have open right now
traps.mechanism: changeItems and ChangeAndSaveItem emit PayloadEmitSource.LocalChanged by default (MutatorService.ts:100-108; ChangeAndSaveItem passes an undefined emitSource). NoteViewController forwards the change, but SuperEditor only loads new text into Lexical when isPayloadSourceRetrieved(source) is true (SuperEditor.tsx:204-216). PlainEditor only resets its local editorText for retrieved sources or note-type changes (PlainEditor.tsx:214-233). NoteView only refreshes the title for retrieved sources (NoteView.tsx:279-292). Retrieved means RemoteRetrieved or ComponentRetrieved only (EmitSource.ts:42-44). So the open editor keeps showing the old text, and the next keystroke saves the editor's stale full text through SuperEditor handleChange (SuperEditor.tsx:171-189) or PlainEditor persistText (PlainEditor.tsx:98-114,249), silently undoing the replacement in that note. The only app code that rewrites an open note's text, restoreRevision, deliberately emits PayloadEmitSource.RemoteRetrieved (NoteHistoryController.ts:321-348).
traps.why_unsignposted: grep -rn RemoteRetrieved packages/web/src returns only NoteHistoryController.ts:346, with no explanatory comment. The only TODO in SuperEditor.tsx, PlainEditor.tsx and NoteSyncController.ts is about bubble unlinking (SuperEditor.tsx:197). The EmitSource.ts doc for LocalChanged says the client 'maps it to update UI', which suggests the UI will refresh.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit tests with mocked mutator or items only check that changeItems got the new text. The editors are never mounted, and Lexical or textarea local state is outside the test.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In the diff, check for a retrieved emit source or an explicit refresh of the active editor. Manually: open a note containing the word, run replace-all, and the editor still shows the old word. Type one character, reopen the note, and the replacement is gone.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: and the notes list should show the updated text
traps.mechanism: The list renders preview_html if present, otherwise preview_plain, and never falls back to text (ListItemNotePreviewText.tsx:10-32). These fields are written only by the editor save paths. The plain path takes the first 160 chars of text in NoteSyncController (NoteSyncController.ts:222-236). For Super notes the editor supplies the preview from the first two Lexical text nodes (SuperEditor.tsx:171-189; SuperEditor/Utils.ts:13-29). The NoteMutator.text setter does not touch previews (NoteMutator.ts:15-29). So setting only text leaves a stale preview. Reusing NoteSyncController-style truncation on a Super note stores raw JSON as the preview. Updating preview_plain without clearing a preview_html written by an iframe editor still shows the old HTML preview.
traps.why_unsignposted: No comment on NoteContent or NoteMutator says previews are derived. grep preview_plain shows only editor or import save paths.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests assert on note.text, not on preview fields, and do not render ListItemNotePreviewText.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Replace a word near the start of a plain note and of a Super note. The list preview still shows the old word, or shows JSON for the Super note.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Skip anything I'm not allowed to edit and tell me what got skipped
traps.mechanism: In this app, 'not allowed to edit' means note.locked OR being a read-only member of the note's shared vault. NoteView makes the editor read-only through vaultUsers.isCurrentUserReadonlyVaultMember (NoteView.tsx:129,885,986), and NotesOptions disables actions with the same check (NotesOptions.tsx:135-137). NotesController only checks note.locked (NotesController.ts:304,375). If the bulk replace checks only locked, edits to read-only shared-vault notes are pushed. The server rejects them with SharedVaultInsufficientPermissionsError, and DeltaRemoteRejected.handleVaultError creates a non-vaulted conflicted duplicate of each edited note while restoring the server version (RemoteRejected.ts:29-36,54-86,154-178). The result is surprise duplicate notes in the user's private space, which the skipped list never mentions.
traps.why_unsignposted: The read-only checks live in UI components only. NoteMutator and ChangeAndSaveItem have no guard. Nothing links locked and vault-readonly in one helper.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: There is no server in unit tests, so the rejection and duplication path never runs.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In the diff, check for a vault read-only check. Manually, as a read-only member of a shared vault (Labs), run replace: duplicates appear in Conflicts, and the note is not reported as skipped.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Skip trashed notes and notes that use other editors (spreadsheets, authenticator and so on)
traps.mechanism: noteType is not authoritative. EditorForNoteUseCase resolves notes whose noteType is undefined through legacy editor associations or a legacy default editor (EditorForNote.ts:17-46,72-92). Note.ts:40-45 sets Plain only for the legacy prefers-plain flag. Export decides the format with componentManager.editorForNote (NoteExportUtils.ts:17-29). A strict noteType whitelist skips every legacy plain or Markdown note. Treating undefined as plain rewrites legacy spreadsheet or token-vault JSON.
traps.why_unsignposted: The noteType field name suggests it is the format. The legacy path is visible only inside the snjs use case.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Test fixtures set noteType explicitly.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In the diff, check whether eligibility uses note.noteType or editorForNote. This trap is contested, because SuperNoteImporter.tsx:40 itself treats a missing noteType as text.

other_criteria: Per-note hit counts shown before confirming, and the counts equal what gets replaced (no JSON keys counted in Super notes)
Super formatting, embeds, links, checklists and so on are unchanged; no lossy Markdown round-trip
Protected notes are excluded unless the protection session is authorized, as with 'include protected contents' in search
Trashed notes are skipped, and the skipped list is shown to the user
Changes sync like normal edits (modified date updated)
ideas.frontend_share: About 100% packages/web: a new modal or controller, plus Super JSON traversal through the Lexical headless editor or HeadlessSuperConverter. It may touch NoteViewController and ItemGroupController to refresh the active editor. No server change.
ideas.risks: The prompt mentions the open note, which may push a careful model to inspect the editor observers and find the RemoteRetrieved pattern. Trap 4 is contested because SuperNoteImporter.tsx:40 uses the lenient pattern. Trap 3 needs the Labs vaults feature and a second account to reproduce by hand (diff reading is enough). Many explicit requirements (protected, trash, Super formatting) are ones the model will handle, so pass or fail rests on traps 1-3.

ideas.title: Copy a note into a (shared) vault, keeping the original private
ideas.prompt: Vaults only let me move a note. I'd like 'Copy to vault' next to it in the note options, so I can drop a copy into one of my vaults (usually a shared one) and keep my original private where it is. The copy should look identical, including embedded images and attachments, and other people in a shared vault need to be able to open them. My original note and its files must keep working exactly as before, whatever later happens to the copy. Tag the copy with the same tag names, but using tags that live in that vault (create them there if missing), and don't move or change any of my existing tags. @-links to notes that aren't in that vault should just become their title as plain text. Protected notes need my password first, and don't offer vaults where I'm read-only.
ideas.background: Vaults (a Labs feature) are separate key systems; shared vaults are shared with contacts. Items in a vault carry key_system_identifier and shared_vault_uuid. The UI only has Move to vault and Move out (AddToVaultMenuOption.tsx), and VaultService.moveItemToVault refuses notes linked to items in other vaults. Files are FileItems (metadata plus encryption key) that point at server bytes through remoteIdentifier, and shared-vault files must sit in vault storage on the server. Super notes embed files as snfile nodes holding fileUuid, and @-links as bubble nodes holding itemUuid, separately from the item references. The feature adds Copy to vault: an independent copy of the note (and its files) inside the target vault.
ideas.gap_evidence: Pin equals upstream HEAD. grep -rni 'copy to vault|copyToVault|copyItemToVault' over packages finds nothing. AddToVaultMenuOption.tsx only calls vaults.moveItemToVault or removeItemFromVault. git log -i --grep 'copy.*vault|duplicate.*vault' finds nothing. VaultService and the UseCase folder have Move and Remove but no Copy.
ideas.natural_implementation: Duplicate the note with mutator.duplicateItem (as Duplicate does at NotesController.ts:661-668), then vaults.moveItemToVault(vault, copy). For attachments, duplicateItem(file) followed by moveItemToVault(vault, fileCopy). For tags, findOrCreateTag(title, vault) plus addTagToNote, or the LinkingController.createAndAddNewTag pattern. Bubbles are converted to text by editing the copied Super JSON.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: other people in a shared vault need to be able to open them. My original note and its files must keep working exactly as before, whatever later happens to the copy
traps.mechanism: PayloadsByDuplicating copies FileItem content unchanged (PayloadsByDuplicating.ts:24-48), so a duplicated file has the same remoteIdentifier and key and points at the same server blob. Moving it into a shared vault runs MoveItemsToVault, which calls files.moveFileToSharedVault (MoveItemsToVault.ts:25-40). That requests a 'user-to-shared-vault' Move valet token for the shared remoteIdentifier (FileService.ts:141-164), which relocates the original's bytes. Skipping the move leaves vault members unable to download, because shared-vault reads need vault storage (FileService.ts downloadFile and createSharedVaultValetToken). In a private vault both items share one blob, and files.deleteFile on the copy deletes it by remoteIdentifier (FileService.ts:396-410). The correct approach is to download with FilesController.getFileBlob (FilesController.ts:306) and re-upload with uploadNewFile using the copy as note, which uses that note's vault (FilesController.ts:489-541).
traps.why_unsignposted: grep -ri duplicat in services/Domain/Files and packages/files finds nothing. duplicateItem has no file special case, and moveItemToVault shows no warning about byte moves.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked files and vault services just record calls, and no server exists to move or delete blobs.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In the diff, check whether file items are duplicated or moved instead of re-uploaded. Manually, after copying into a shared vault, download the original's attachment: it fails. Or delete the copy's file in a private vault, and the original's file breaks.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: The copy should look identical, including embedded images and attachments, and other people in a shared vault need to be able to open them
traps.mechanism: Super embeds store fileUuid inside the node JSON (SerializedFileNode.tsx; read via HeadlessSuperConverter.getEmbeddedFileIDsFromSuperString at HeadlessSuperConverter.tsx:290-310), independent of the file-to-note reference. After re-uploading new FileItems, the copied JSON still points at the original private file uuids. The owner sees images fine because they can decrypt the originals. Vault members see missing files.
traps.why_unsignposted: No helper remaps embed ids. Linking APIs touch references only.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests run as the owner or mock findItem, so embeds resolve.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: In the diff, check that fileUuid in the copied Super JSON is rewritten to the new file uuids. Manually, a second vault member opens the copy and the embeds are missing.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Tag the copy with the same tag names, but using tags that live in that vault (create them there if missing), and don't move or change any of my existing tags
traps.mechanism: findOrCreateTag(title, createInVault) calls findOrCreateTagByTitle, then ItemManager.findTagByTitleAndParent, which searches root tags by title regardless of vault (ItemManager.ts:645-651; MutatorService.ts:533-541,583-585). The vault argument is used only when creating. So the user's private 'Work' tag is returned, and addTagToNote then fails with a 'different vaults' alert (MutatorService.ts:644-651). The in-app precedent LinkingController.createAndAddNewTag works around this by moving the found tag into the item's vault (LinkingController.tsx:302-327), which violates 'don't move my tags'. findOrCreateTagParentChain has no vault parameter, which matters for nested tags (MutatorService.ts:449-461).
traps.why_unsignposted: The parameter name createInVault reads like 'scope to vault'. No comment says lookup ignores vaults.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Fixtures rarely have a same-named tag outside the vault, and mocked mutators return whatever is asked.
