ideas.title: Per-panel time range and refresh interval on dashboards
ideas.prompt: Can we get per-panel time settings on dashboards? On our ops dashboard I want a few panels locked to, say, the last 7 days and refreshing every 10 minutes, while everything else follows the dashboard's time picker and its 30-second auto-refresh. In edit mode the panel menu should let me set a custom range (same quick ranges and date format as the main picker) and optionally a refresh interval, show a small badge with the panel's range, and let me reset it to follow the dashboard again. A panel with its own interval should refresh only on that schedule. This has to survive saving and sharing the dashboard and work for every panel type we use: regular visualizations, TSVB, Timeline, saved searches, and the PPL visualizations we add from the new Discover. In a panel with its own range, the time axis labels should fit that range, and drag-to-zoom should zoom just that panel, not the whole dashboard.
ideas.background: OSD dashboards are embeddable containers. DashboardContainer.getInheritedInput (src/plugins/dashboard/public/application/embeddable/dashboard_container.tsx:254-264) passes timeRange, refreshConfig, query and filters to every child panel. Container.getInputForChild (src/plugins/embeddable/public/lib/containers/container.ts:130-157) lets a panel's explicitInput override inherited keys. explicitInput is persisted as the panel's embeddableConfig (src/plugins/dashboard/public/application/utils/embeddable_saved_object_converters.ts:65) and so also lands in the dashboard URL/app state (create_dashboard_container.tsx:432-489). The feature: a panel context-menu action plus a PANEL_BADGE_TRIGGER badge. The action writes a per-panel timeRange (and refresh interval) into explicitInput; reset removes it. Each embeddable type must then honour these for its data, axis, refresh cadence and brushing. Kibana's 2019 x-pack implementation (commit 5eb8cfb243 'Per panel time range', x-pack/legacy/plugins/advanced_ui_actions) is in git history but x-pack is not in the OSD tree, and it predates PPL, the explore plugin and the OSD Timeline/TSVB code.
ideas.gap_evidence: At pin and at upstream HEAD d0e068f237 (2026-11-04): grep -rn 'CUSTOM_TIME_RANGE|customTimeRange|custom time range|CustomTimeRange' src finds only a leftover disabled-action id string in dashboard_container.tsx (showPlaceholderUntil, ~line 274 at HEAD) and a prose paragraph in src/plugins/embeddable/docs/input_and_output_state.md:110-140. There is no action, badge or flyout. The dashboard actions dir at HEAD has only add_to_library, clone_panel, expand_panel, library_notification, move_panel_to_section, replace_panel and unlink_from_library. No plugin registers anything on PANEL_BADGE_TRIGGER, and src/plugins has no ui_actions_enhanced or advanced_ui_actions. grep refreshConfig shows no embeddable reading input.refreshConfig; only the dashboard container and content_management set it. git log --grep='Per panel time range' (pin and FETCH_HEAD) returns only the 2019 Kibana x-pack commit 5eb8cfb243, whose files are absent from the tree. No setting or labs flag covers this.
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Create a CustomizePanelTimeRangeAction (CONTEXT_MENU_TRIGGER, edit mode only) that opens a flyout or modal with EuiSuperDatePicker. Feed it commonlyUsedRanges from timepicker:quickRanges and dateFormat, copied from the data plugin's QueryBarTopRow, plus an EuiRefreshInterval. 2) On apply, call embeddable.updateInput({ timeRange, refreshConfig }), which flows into panels[id].explicitInput and then embeddableConfig. Reset calls updateInput({ timeRange: undefined }). 3) Add a PANEL_BADGE_TRIGGER badge that uses prettyDuration to show the range when explicitInput.timeRange is set (the pattern in embeddable/docs/input_and_output_state.md). 4) For the panel's own refresh interval, start a per-panel setInterval in the action or container that calls child.reload(). 5) For drag-to-zoom, register an action on SELECT_RANGE_TRIGGER (events.ts maps 'brush' to it) that is compatible when the panel has an explicit timeRange and calls updateInput with the brushed range, and make ACTION_SELECT_RANGE skip such panels. 6) Unit tests with a mocked container and embeddable to check that explicitInput gets set, the badge shows, and the reset works. All of these pass.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: work for every panel type we use: ... and the PPL visualizations we add from the new Discover
traps.mechanism: The explore embeddable looks correct. It builds its time filter from this.input.timeRange (src/plugins/explore/public/embeddable/explore_embeddable.tsx:188-191) and refetches only when input.timeRange changes (285-300). But with query enhancements on, search_service.ts:166-176 routes the fetch by query language to PPLSearchInterceptor, and that interceptor ignores the searchSource time filter. It builds the WHERE time clause from the GLOBAL timefilter: query_enhancements/public/search/ppl_search_interceptor.ts:139-145 calls getTimeFilterWhereClause(dataset.timeFieldName, this.queryService.timefilter.timefilter.getTime()). It also injects the global time into request.params.body.timeRange at 85-95, and getAggConfig at 156-159 also reads global time. SQL does the same (sql_search_interceptor.ts:76), as does PromQL (promql_search_interceptor.ts:34). A PPL panel set to 'last 7 days' on a 15-minute dashboard therefore queries 15 minutes, and does not refetch when the dashboard time later changes. The same applies to classic saved searches written in PPL.
traps.why_unsignposted: No comment in explore_embeddable.tsx mentions that the interceptor overrides time. grep -i 'embeddable|panel|dashboard|global' in ppl_search_interceptor.ts and sql_search_interceptor.ts finds only the filterManagerSupportedAppNames=['dashboards'] constant (line 33), nothing about time. The only nearby test (ppl_search_interceptor.test.ts) expects the timefilter value. Nothing ties the input.timeRange path to the interceptor.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: A natural test for the explore embeddable mocks searchSource.fetch and checks that the time filter function returns getTime(indexPattern, input.timeRange). That passes, because the override happens later inside the search service and the interceptor, which unit tests mock away. Checking it live needs OpenSearch with the SQL/PPL plugin, which the model is unlikely to set up.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Read the diff. If query_enhancements' PPL/SQL interceptors (or the explore embeddable's fetch) were not changed to take the panel's time range (e.g. via request.params.body.timeRange or a search option), the requirement is violated. Manual check: in an Observability workspace, add a PPL explore visualization to a dashboard set to 'Last 15 minutes', give the panel 'Last 7 days', and compare its row count or chart extent with Discover over 7 days, or inspect the PPL request's WHERE clause.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: drag-to-zoom should zoom just that panel, not the whole dashboard
traps.mechanism: Only vislib brushing goes through SELECT_RANGE_TRIGGER (visualizations/public/embeddable/events.ts:40,47; vislib vis_controller.tsx:96). TSVB, Timeline and Vega brushes instead fire an applyFilter event with a timeFieldName '*' range filter: TSVB application/lib/create_brush_handler.ts:33-49 (wired in vis_editor.js:64), Timeline components/timeline_vis_component.tsx:404-420 (plotselected), Vega vega_view/vega_base_view.js:396-414 (setTimeFilterHandler). VisualizeEmbeddable sends these to APPLY_FILTER_TRIGGER (visualize_embeddable.ts:353-373), and ACTION_GLOBAL_APPLY_FILTER then calls changeTimeFilter on the GLOBAL timefilter (data/public/actions/apply_filter_action.ts:109-117). An override registered on SELECT_RANGE_TRIGGER works for area/line/bar charts, but brushing a TSVB or Timeline panel with its own range still changes the whole dashboard's time.
traps.why_unsignposted: events.ts maps brush to SELECT_RANGE_TRIGGER, which suggests brushing is one path. Nothing in select_range_action.ts or apply_filter_action.ts says that some vis types encode brushes as '*' range filters through applyFilter. create_brush_handler.ts has no comment about which trigger it reaches.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests of the new SELECT_RANGE action with a mocked context and embeddable pass. Nobody writes a test that fires a TSVB or Timeline applyFilter brush through the real VisualizeEmbeddable event mapping.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Give a TSVB time-series panel (or a Timeline panel) a custom range and brush across it. If the dashboard's time picker changes, or the panel range does not change, it fails. In the diff, check whether the APPLY_FILTER_TRIGGER/'*' time-filter path is handled for panels with an explicit timeRange.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: In a panel with its own range, the time axis labels should fit that range ... (panel types include) Timeline
traps.mechanism: Timeline fetches correctly with the context timeRange (vis_type_timeline/public/helpers/timeline_request_handler.ts:81-123), but it renders the x-axis tick format from the GLOBAL timefilter. buildOptions (helpers/panel_utils.ts:117-133) calls timefilter.getBounds() and computes calculateInterval(min, max, ..., 'auto') from it (common/lib/calculate_interval.ts:72-90). xaxisFormatterProvider (helpers/xaxis_formatter.ts:36-58) then picks the dateFormat:scaled pattern from that interval. The timefilter passed in is opensearchDashboards.services.timefilter (timeline_vis_component.tsx:211-216, from plugin.ts:98), i.e. the global one. Result: on a 15-minute dashboard, a Timeline panel set to 'last 7 days' gets ticks formatted 'HH:mm:ss' with no dates. Vislib, XY and TSVB derive axis formats from the agg or response interval, so they are correct, which makes Timeline the odd one out.
traps.why_unsignposted: panel_utils.ts:124 only says '// Get the X-axis tick format'. Nothing says the bounds come from the global time rather than the request. The data path, which a model checks first, is correct.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: buildOptions is internal, and existing Timeline tests do not cover axis formatting against a timeRange different from the global one. A model that checks Timeline only verifies that the request uses timeRange.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Dashboard on 'Last 15 minutes'. A Timeline panel with expression .es(*) and interval auto, given a custom 'Last 7 days': the axis ticks show only times (e.g. 00:00:00), not dates. In the diff, buildOptions or the Timeline component still read timefilter.getBounds().

traps.requirement_in_prompt: A panel with its own interval should refresh only on that schedule.
traps.mechanism: Dashboard auto-refresh does not flow through container input. The global Timefilter runs window.setInterval and emits autoRefreshFetch$ (data/public/query/timefilter/timefilter.ts:166-172). Each embeddable subscribes to it directly and refetches on every tick: visualize_embeddable.ts:187-189, discover search_embeddable.tsx:159-161, explore_embeddable.tsx:166-172, vis_builder_embeddable.tsx:126-128. No embeddable reads input.refreshConfig (grep refreshConfig). A per-panel timer calling reload() therefore adds refreshes, but a panel set to 'every 10 minutes' still refetches on every 30-second dashboard tick, across four embeddable classes.
traps.why_unsignposted: refreshConfig is part of the inherited input (dashboard_container.tsx:261), which suggests it controls children, but nothing consumes it. The subscriptions have no comments.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests with fake timers check that the per-panel timer calls reload() at the chosen interval. They do not emit the global autoRefreshFetch$, so the extra refetches stay invisible.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Set the dashboard to a 5s auto-refresh and one panel to 1 minute, and watch the Inspect > Requests count or the network tab for that panel. The diff must suppress or replace the global autoRefreshFetch$ subscription for overridden panels in every embeddable type (visualize, search, explore, vis_builder).

other_criteria: Action shown only in edit mode via the panel context menu; picker uses timepicker:quickRanges and dateFormat like the main picker
Optional per-panel refresh interval control
Badge on overridden panels shows the panel range; badge or menu offers reset to follow the dashboard
Panel overrides persist in the saved dashboard (panelsJSON embeddableConfig) and in shared/snapshot URLs
Classic visualizations, TSVB, Timeline data and saved-search panels fetch with the panel range
Dashboard time changes leave overridden panels alone; non-overridden panels keep following the dashboard
ideas.frontend_share: ~100% frontend: new action and badge (dashboard or embeddable public), changes to VisualizeEmbeddable, SearchEmbeddable, ExploreEmbeddable and VisBuilderEmbeddable refresh handling, Timeline component options, brush/apply-filter routing (data/public/actions or a dashboard-level action), and passing the time range through query_enhancements' public PPL/SQL interceptors. No server changes needed.
ideas.risks: The 2019 Kibana per-panel time range commit (5eb8cfb243) is in git history and gives the model the action, badge and modal design, so the core UI is easy. A very thorough model might grep all timefilter.getTime()/getBounds()/getAutoRefreshFetch$ uses and catch several traps at once (the traps are correlated through that grep). PPL panels need QE plus the explore plugin, and a full manual check needs OpenSearch with the SQL plugin, though reading the diff is enough. Upstream HEAD later added a request-level timeRange override in ppl_search_interceptor (HEAD ~line 199, 'Prefer an explicit time range passed and fall back to the global timefilter'), which is not at the pin but shows the fix shape. The prompt is long and lists many requirements, so a reviewer could see it as two features (time + refresh).

ideas.title: 'View in Discover' action for dashboard panels
ideas.prompt: Could you add a 'View in Discover' item to the panel menu on dashboards? It should open Discover showing exactly the documents that panel is built from: same index pattern, the dashboard's current time range, query and filters (pinned ones stay pinned, disabled ones stay off), plus any query or filters saved on the visualization itself or on the saved search it's based on, so the hit count in Discover matches what the panel counts. For saved-search panels, open that saved search with the dashboard's query and filters applied on top. It should be there in both view and edit mode, but not on panels Discover can't reproduce, like text, TSVB, Vega or Timeline panels. Using it shouldn't change anything on the dashboard itself.
ideas.background: OSD has no 'explore underlying data' style action. The discover plugin registers a Kibana-era DiscoverUrlGenerator (src/plugins/discover/public/url_generator.ts, registered in plugin.ts:173-180, no consumers in the repo) that builds legacy '#/...?_g&_a' URLs. On mount, the discover app migrates these with migrateUrlState (migrate_state.ts) into data-explorer's _a/_q/_g. A panel's effective documents are defined by the expression function opensearch_dashboards_context (src/plugins/expressions/common/expression_functions/specs/opensearch_dashboards_context.ts:99-130). It merges container input query and filters with the vis's own saved q/filters (build_pipeline.ts:393-406) and the linked saved search's query and filters. Saved-search panels AND the saved search's own query with the dashboard query through parent searchSources (search_embeddable.tsx:231-240, 391-392; search_source.ts:586-587 concatenates queries). Kibana's 2020 x-pack implementation (commit cab833e219, x-pack/plugins/discover_enhanced) is in git history.
ideas.gap_evidence: At pin and HEAD d0e068f237: grep -rni 'explore underlying|EXPLORE_DATA|view in discover|open in discover' src/plugins finds only explore's trace-logs button 'View in Discover Logs' (explore/.../trace_details/public/logs/dataset_accordion_list.tsx:94) and an agent_traces notice. Nothing in dashboard or embeddable panel actions. The dashboard actions dir (HEAD) has no such action. git grep DISCOVER_APP_URL_GENERATOR finds no consumer outside discover itself. git log --grep='Explore underlying data' returns only Kibana-era x-pack commits (cab833e219, 8788928218, 9303747b54, c0f4f1d7d2), and x-pack is absent from the tree. The existing 'Edit' action for saved-search panels opens the saved search without any dashboard context.
ideas.natural_implementation: Follow Kibana's ExploreDataContextMenuAction (in history): a CONTEXT_MENU_TRIGGER action. isCompatible checks embeddable.getOutput().indexPatterns.length > 0, and Kibana's version also requires viewMode === VIEW. execute takes { timeRange, query, filters } from embeddable.getInput() and indexPatternId from output.indexPatterns[0].id, calls discover.urlGenerator.createUrl({ indexPatternId, filters, query, timeRange }) and navigates. For saved-search panels it passes savedSearchId to the same generator, or builds '#/view/<id>' with the dashboard's query and filters in the URL. The prompt asks for the vis's own query and filters, so add vis.data.searchSource.getField('query'/'filter') to the filters, and/or concatenate the queries. Unit tests assert on the generated URL (like url_generator.test.ts) with mocked embeddables.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: For saved-search panels, open that saved search with the dashboard's query and filters applied on top ... so the hit count in Discover matches what the panel counts
traps.mechanism: Both natural routes break. (a) DiscoverUrlGenerator.createUrl({ savedSearchId }) builds appBasePath + '#/' + id (url_generator.ts:108,128). migrateUrlState then checks '#/context', '#/doc', '#/view/:id' and finally '#/' (migrate_state.ts:69-110). '#/<id>' matches only the bare '#/' pattern, so params.id is undefined and Discover opens WITHOUT the saved search: its query, filters and columns are dropped. (b) The working route '#/view/<id>' (savedSearches.urlFor) with the dashboard query in _q goes through use_search.ts:550-556, where loadSavedSearch replaces the saved search's own query with the URL query whenever the URL query is not the default ('query = isDataQueryDefault ? savedSearchQuery ?? dataQuery : dataQuery'). The panel ANDs both queries (search_embeddable.tsx:391-392 sets the dashboard query on the parent searchSource; search_source.ts:586-587 merges them), so Discover returns more hits than the panel whenever the dashboard has a query. Correct behaviour needs the saved search's query kept and the dashboard query (or one of them) turned into a filter.
traps.why_unsignposted: url_generator.ts documents 'savedSearchId?: Optionally set saved search ID.' and url_generator.test.ts:73-76 asserts startsWith(appBasePath + '#/' + savedSearchId) as if that were correct. migrate_state.ts has only a generic 'TODO: Write unit tests once all routes have been migrated.' Nothing on the dashboard side, or in the generator, says the saved-search URL is dead or that the URL query replaces the saved search's query. (The comment at use_search.ts:555 sits inside Discover's loader, downstream of the natural path.)
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit tests assert that the generated URL contains the saved search id and the dashboard query, encoding the same assumption as url_generator.test.ts. Only actually loading Discover shows the dropped saved search or query.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Create a saved search with query geo.src:CN on a dashboard whose query is machine.os:ios. Use View in Discover and compare the Discover hit count with the panel's. With (a) no saved search is loaded; with (b) the query bar shows only machine.os:ios and the counts differ. In the diff, look for '#/<id>' generator use, or for passing the dashboard query as the URL query alongside '#/view/<id>'.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: plus any query or filters saved on the visualization itself or on the saved search it's based on, so the hit count in Discover matches what the panel counts
traps.mechanism: The panel's real context is input plus the vis's own q/filters plus the saved search's query/filters (opensearch_dashboards_context.ts:99-130, build_pipeline.ts:393-406). Kibana's reference action (git show cab833e219, explore_data_context_menu_action.ts:196-203) uses only embeddable.getInput(). If the model reads the vis's searchSource it still has to (1) walk to the linked saved search (vis.data.savedSearchId or the parent searchSource) and (2) merge two queries into Discover's single query slot, even when the vis was saved with Lucene and the dashboard uses DQL. String concatenation or picking one silently changes the result set; one query has to become a filter (e.g. built with buildOpenSearchQuery or buildQueryFilter).
traps.why_unsignposted: VisualizeEmbeddable has no getter or comment for the effective query. The only place that composes it is the expression function, which a model building a URL does not read. The Kibana precedent in history uses getInput() only.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked embeddables in unit tests have one query language and no linked saved search, so URL-shape assertions pass.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Build a vis on a saved search (query response:404) with its own Lucene query extension:jpg and a saved filter, and put it on a dashboard with the DQL query machine.os:win*. Discover's hit count must equal the panel's Count metric. Check the generated Discover state for all three parts and the language handling.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: not on panels Discover can't reproduce, like text, TSVB, Vega or Timeline panels
traps.mechanism: The natural compatibility check, embeddable.getOutput().indexPatterns.length > 0 (Kibana's isOutputWithIndexPatterns), assumes non-index-pattern vis types report none. But createVisEmbeddableFromObject fills indexPatterns from vis.type.getUsedIndexPattern (create_vis_embeddable_from_object.ts:84-88). TSVB implements it with indexPatterns.find(params.index_pattern) (vis_type_timeseries/public/metrics_type.ts:120-124), and Vega extracts index patterns from the spec (vis_type_vega/public/vega_type.ts:80-88). So the action shows on TSVB and Vega panels, where Discover cannot reproduce per-series or spec queries.
traps.why_unsignposted: No comment on getUsedIndexPattern says it is used for embeddable output. The name implies 'used for display' and the type's docs do not mention action compatibility.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests use mocked embeddables with hand-set outputs: a markdown one with indexPatterns [] and a line chart with one.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Open the panel menu on a TSVB panel and a Vega panel that query a real index pattern title: 'View in Discover' must not appear.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: It should be there in both view and edit mode
traps.mechanism: Kibana's reference (cab833e219 explore_data_context_menu_action.ts:163) returns false when viewMode !== VIEW. A model that follows the precedent from git log inherits an edit-mode exclusion.
traps.why_unsignposted: The check sits in the historical reference with the commit note 'fix: disable action in edit mode', which presents it as intended behaviour.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests copied from the reference assert the same view-mode gating.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Switch the dashboard to edit mode and open the panel menu: the item must be present.

other_criteria: Pinned dashboard filters arrive as pinned (global) filters in Discover, disabled ones stay disabled
Discover opens with the dashboard's current time range
Classic visualization panels open on the panel's index pattern
Using the action does not mutate dashboard state (filters, query, time) when you come back
