ideas.title: Read-only and No-download badges on Files rows, consistent across All files and the Shares views
ideas.prompt: Could you add small badges to rows in the Files list? 'Read-only' on files I can't edit and on folders I can't add anything to, and 'No download' on things shared with me where downloading is turned off. The badges are about what I can do, so files in my own storage never get one, even ones I've shared with others with restrictions for them. It has to be consistent: an item shows the same badges whether I see it in All files, Recent, Favorites, search results or under Shares (Shared with you, Shared with others, Shared by link). Example: Anna shares a single document with me directly as view-only, so it's read-only everywhere; if her team group, which I'm in, also gets it with edit rights, it's editable everywhere, same as when I open it. No badges for public-link visitors or in Deleted files.
ideas.background: The Files app (apps/files/src, Vue 2.7 legacy frontend) renders each row from an @nextcloud/files Node and shows per-row indicators through inline file actions (apps/files_sharing/src/files_actions/sharingStatusAction.ts, apps/files_reminders/src/files_actions/reminderStatusAction.ts, apps/comments/src/actions/inlineUnreadCommentsAction.ts). Nodes come from two different sources: (1) WebDAV (All files, Recent, Favorites, search, tags) via @nextcloud/files resultToNode(), which converts the DAV permission string (e.g. 'SRGDNVW') into a bitmask with parsePermissions(); (2) the OCS share API for the Shares views (apps/files_sharing/src/files_views/shares.ts -> services/SharingService.ts ocsEntryToNode()), which copies OCS share fields straight into Node.permissions and Node.attributes. The feature is one or two new inline status actions: 'Read-only' when the current user cannot change a file's content or cannot create inside a folder, and 'No download' when a received share disables download; hidden on public share pages and in the trashbin view.
ideas.gap_evidence: At pin c8e2bb93 and upstream HEAD a3222e16: git grep -i 'read-only|read only|view-only|view only|no download|download disabled|cannot edit' over apps/files/src, apps/files_sharing/src/files_actions, files_views, services returns only an unrelated comment (FileEntryMixin.ts:364 at pin) and, at HEAD, ReferenceFileWidget.vue preview comments. Inline actions that exist (grep 'inline:' in apps/*/src): sharingStatusAction, reminderStatusAction, inlineUnreadCommentsAction, accept/reject/restoreShareAction, enterCredentialsAction, trashbin restoreAction - none shows the user's access level. No user setting covers it: UserConfig keys (apps/files/src/types.ts:56-68: crop_image_previews, default_view, folder_tree, grid_view, sort_*, show_files_extensions, show_hidden, show_mime_column, show_dialog_*). git log origin/master -i -E --grep='read-only (badge|indicator|icon)|permission (badge|indicator)' returns nothing. Upstream feat commits since the pin touching files/files_sharing (sidebar API, unified sharing dialog behind sharing.unified_api_enable, tag filter, reference widget) do not add it; SharingService.ts at HEAD still maps permissions from item_permissions and still merges duplicates with nodes[0].
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Add apps/files/src/actions/accessBadgeAction.ts (or two actions) copied from sharingStatusAction.ts: inline: () => true, enabled({nodes, view}) => nodes.length === 1 && !isPublicShare() && view.id !== 'trashbin' && isReadOnly(nodes[0]), displayName/title 'Read-only', lock icon, exec returns null. 2) isReadOnly(node): folder -> !(node.permissions & Permission.CREATE); file -> !(node.permissions & Permission.WRITE) (per the @nextcloud/files Permission doc 'Can change the file content', and isSyncable in apps/files/src/utils/permissions.ts:52) or !(node.permissions & Permission.UPDATE) (per FileInfo.canEdit in files_sharing/src/services/FileInfo.ts:73-75, VersionEntry hasUpdatePermissions, renameAction); possibly an early return when node.owner === getCurrentUser().uid. 3) 'No download' action: enabled when !isDownloadable(node), reusing apps/files/src/utils/permissions.ts:17-39 exactly as downloadAction.ts:42 does. 4) Register both in apps/files/src/init.ts, add a little CSS, write vitest specs that build new File/Folder nodes with permission masks and share-attributes and assert enabled().

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Anna shares a single document with me directly as view-only, so it's read-only everywhere
traps.mechanism: If the file check uses Permission.UPDATE (the 'edit' bit in this repo's neighbours: FileInfo.canEdit() files_sharing/src/services/FileInfo.ts:73-75, VersionEntry.vue:242-244 hasUpdatePermissions gating restore, bulkSystemTagsAction.ts:53, and server semantics in SharePermissionsToolBox.js:6-21 where ALL_FILE = UPDATE|READ|SHARE), it is wrong for share mount roots. @nextcloud/files 4.0.0 parsePermissions maps DAV 'NV' (rename+move) to UPDATE and 'W' to WRITE (lib/dav/davPermissions.ts:19-36). For the root of every movable mount the server adds UPDATE|DELETE in directory listings (lib/private/Files/View.php:1650-1657) and canRename() is always true (lib/public/Files/DavUtil.php:55-60, 84-88), while 'W' is computed from the real share permission (DavUtil.php:62-75, comment 'since we always add update permissions for the root of movable mounts'). A view-only file shared directly therefore arrives as 'SMGDNV' -> READ|UPDATE|DELETE, so the badge is missing. The same happens for a view-only folder share root if UPDATE is used for folders too, and writable admin-mounted external storage roots lose UPDATE (View.php:1655-1656) and get flagged as read-only.
traps.why_unsignposted: No frontend file mentions that mount roots carry NV; grep for DAV permission fixtures like 'SGNV', 'SMGDNV', 'RGDNV' in apps/*/src and core/src finds none. The only explanation is a PHP comment in DavUtil.php that a frontend implementer has no reason to open. The repo's own 'canEdit' helper actively points at UPDATE.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: The natural spec builds new File({ permissions: Permission.READ }) for 'view-only' and READ|UPDATE|WRITE for 'editable'; both pass. Only a real DAV string for a share mount root ('SMGDNV') would expose it, and no such fixture exists.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Read the predicate: if it uses UPDATE for files (or ORs UPDATE in), feed it parsePermissions('SMGDNV'). Manual: user A shares one file view-only with user B; as B, All files shows the file without a Read-only badge.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: files in my own storage never get one, even ones I've shared with others ... an item shows the same badges whether I see it in All files ... or under Shares (Shared with you, Shared with others, Shared by link)
traps.mechanism: Shares-view nodes are built with permissions: ocsEntry?.item_permissions || ocsEntry?.permissions (apps/files_sharing/src/services/SharingService.ts:97). These are server Constants (lib/public/Constants.php:23-49: UPDATE=2 means content write, CREATE=4). For my own shares item_permissions = node permissions (apps/files_sharing/lib/Controller/ShareAPIController.php:173-176) and files never get CREATE (lib/private/Files/Storage/Common.php:127-132), so an own file is 27 (also the fixture in SharingService.spec.ts:208/375). For received shares it is the share permission plus DELETE/UPDATE adjustments (ShareAPIController.php:178-191). In @nextcloud/files, Permission.WRITE === Permission.CREATE === 4 (lib/permissions.ts:25-29) and is the bit DAV sets for 'W'. A DAV-correct WRITE check therefore marks every own file in Shared with others / Shared by link as Read-only and every editable received file in Shared with you as Read-only, while All files shows them editable. Any single bit predicate fails either this trap or the previous one.
traps.why_unsignposted: Nothing at SharingService.ts:97 says the ints use different semantics; the @nextcloud/files NodeData doc says permissions is 'A binary mask of Permission values' (lib/node/nodeData.ts:63-67), and the numeric values of the Permission enum match the OCS ints, so they look compatible. The spec only asserts toBe(27) with no explanation.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests construct nodes with DAV-style masks. Catching it requires pushing a realistic OCS entry through getContents() and asserting no badge for an own file, which a mocked badge test would not do.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: As the owner, open Shares > Shared with others: own shared files show Read-only. Or as a recipient of an editable file share, Shared with you shows Read-only while All files does not. In the diff: no special handling of OCS-built nodes.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: if her team group, which I'm in, also gets it with edit rights, it's editable everywhere, same as when I open it
traps.mechanism: OCS shared_with_me returns user shares before group shares (ShareAPIController.php:847-854). SharingService groups entries by source and keeps nodes[0], merging only share-types (SharingService.ts:265-271), so the Shared with you node carries the direct view-only share's permissions and share-attributes. The real mount uses a 'super share' whose permissions are OR-ed and attributes merged into the most permissive combination (apps/files_sharing/lib/MountProvider.php:104-158), which is what DAV (All files) and opening the file reflect. The badge shows Read-only (and possibly No download) only in Shared with you.
traps.why_unsignposted: The comment above the merge says 'Merge duplicate shares and group their attributes', which suggests attributes are combined; nothing warns that permissions and attributes come from just the first share.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked tests use one node per file; nobody feeds two OCS entries for the same path with different permissions.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Share a file to B directly view-only and to a group containing B with edit; as B compare All files (no badge) with Shares > Shared with you (badge). In code, check whether duplicate entries' permissions/attributes are combined.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: files in my own storage never get one, even ones I've shared with others with restrictions for them
traps.mechanism: The natural 'No download' check is the existing isDownloadable() (apps/files/src/utils/permissions.ts:17-39), the same one downloadAction.ts:42 uses: it returns false for attributes['hide-download'] or a share-attributes download=false entry. In DAV these props describe the share through which I access the node and are empty for my own storage (apps/dav/lib/Connector/Sabre/FilesPlugin.php:350-352 and 425-436; Node.php:287-305 only reads ISharedStorage). In the Shares views they are filled from the share record itself (SharingService.ts:102 'hide-download': ocsEntry.hide_download === 1, :107 'share-attributes': ocsEntry.attributes; ShareAPIController.php:338-342). In Shared with others / Shared by link those are the restrictions I set for recipients or link visitors, so my own files get No download there.
traps.why_unsignposted: The existing download action has the same behaviour, so copying it looks correct; no comment distinguishes 'my access' from 'the share I created'.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests set share-attributes download=false on a node and expect the badge, which encodes the 'received share' assumption.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Share an own file with a user with download disabled, or by link with Hide download; open Shared with others / Shared by link as the owner and look for No download on it.

other_criteria: Read-only badge on files whose content I can't change and on folders I can't create in; no badge on editable items
No download badge on received items with download disabled (files inside such a shared folder too)
No badges on public share pages (isPublicShare) and in the trashbin view
Badges have an accessible label/tooltip and are translated with t()
Works in list rows of All files, Recent, Favorites, search and the three Shares views
ideas.frontend_share: 100% frontend: a new action file (apps/files/src/actions or apps/files_sharing/src/files_actions), registration in init.ts, small CSS, possibly a fix in apps/files_sharing/src/services/SharingService.ts (combining duplicate entries, interpreting OCS permissions) or refetching DAV props for share-view nodes. No backend change needed.
ideas.risks: A strong model that reads SharingService closely may decide to refetch real DAV properties for Shares-view nodes (fetchNode per item), which passes the OCS, merge and outgoing-attribute traps in one move; it may also reuse the realistic fixtures in SharingService.spec.ts (item_permissions 27 for an own file) and spot the bit mismatch. A reviewer may count the OCS permission trap and the outgoing-attribute trap as one root cause (share views are OCS-based). The 'same as when I open it' wording relies on DAV permissions being the ground truth, since the editors (Text/Office) are not in this repo. Grid view rendering of inline actions cannot be graded. Upstream is reworking the sharing sidebar (behind sharing.unified_api_enable), but SharingService and ShareAPIController semantics are unchanged at a3222e16.

ideas.title: 'What's using my space' storage breakdown opened from the quota entry in Files
ideas.prompt: My quota keeps filling up and I can't tell what's eating it. Could you make the storage entry at the bottom of the Files navigation open a 'What's using my space' view? List my top-level folders and files by how much of my quota they use, biggest first, with the size and the percentage of my used space, and clicking a folder should break it down the same way. Below that, show my 25 biggest individual files anywhere in my storage. Only count things that actually use my quota: folders other people shared with me and external storages don't, so they must never appear in the biggest-files list or add to any folder's number, even when I've moved a shared folder inside one of my own folders. Hidden files do count, even if I've hidden them in the list.
ideas.background: The Files navigation shows a quota entry (apps/files/src/components/NavigationQuota.vue) fed by initial state 'storageStats' (:54) and GET /apps/files/api/v1/stats (:130), which reports only the user's home storage usage (apps/files/lib/Controller/ApiController.php:365-370 -> OC_Helper::getStorageInfo, lib/private/legacy/OC_Helper.php:174-180 builds rootInfo with includeMountPoints=false). Folder sizes in the file list come from the WebDAV oc:size property, and the app can run WebDAV SEARCH (apps/files/src/services/WebDavSearch.ts, Recent.ts). Received shares, federated shares and external storages are separate mounts placed inside the user's tree; the user can move a received share into any of their folders. The feature is a new view or dialog listing items by home-storage usage, with drill-down and a top-25 biggest-files list, using only existing WebDAV and OCS APIs.
ideas.gap_evidence: At pin and upstream HEAD a3222e16, git grep -i 'biggest|largest files|storage usage|space usage|breakdown' over apps/*/src and core/src returns nothing; NavigationQuota.vue only displays used/total and refreshes. There is no Files view with this purpose (views registered in apps/files/src/init.ts:56-63: favorites, files, personal, recent, search, folder tree) and no setting or app in the server repo for it. Frontend SEARCH bodies never use oc:owner-id (git grep 'owner-id' apps/files/src/services at both commits finds nothing).
ideas.natural_implementation: 1) Make NavigationQuota clickable and open a modal or register a new View (Navigation.register like views/recent.ts). 2) Load the root with the existing getContents/defaultGetContents (PROPFIND depth 1 with getDefaultPropfind, which already includes oc:size and nc:mount-type), drop children whose attributes['mount-type'] is 'shared'/'external' (or is-mount-root true), sort by node.size, and compute percentages against storageStats.used. 3) Drill-down: same PROPFIND for the clicked folder, same filter. 4) Biggest files: client.search with a WebDavSearch-style body, ordered by oc:size descending, limit 25, filtering out directories and then dropping results whose mount-type is shared/external.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: they must never ... add to any folder's number, even when I've moved a shared folder inside one of my own folders
traps.mechanism: The oc:size returned by PROPFIND for a folder includes the sizes of every mount nested inside it. View::getDirectoryContent adds the root size of a mount that sits deeper than a direct child to that child folder ('mountpoint inside subfolder add size to the correct folder', lib/private/Files/View.php:1613-1645), and FileInfo::getSize(includeMounts = true) sums sub-mount roots (lib/private/Files/FileInfo.php:159-171, 300-313, 323-336). Filtering mount roots by nc:mount-type only removes mounts that are direct children of the listed folder, so 'Documents' still includes a received share at 'Documents/Client X/Shared'. Correct options: subtract nested mounts found via OCS shared_with_me/remote_shares (file_target, mountpoint) and the files_external user mount lists, or use SEARCH limited to the home storage (next trap), whose folder nodes have no sub-mounts (FileInfo subMounts only set by View::getFileInfo, FileInfo.php:297).
traps.why_unsignposted: No frontend code or comment says folder sizes include nested mounts; FilesListTableFooter.vue even shows currentFolder.size as the total without caveat. The only explanation is in core PHP (View.php) that a frontend implementer would not read.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Mocked PROPFIND results carry whatever size the test author assumes (own content only), so the sums look right.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Receive a share, move it into a subfolder of one of your own folders, open the breakdown: that folder's number and percentage include the share. In code: sizes taken from PROPFIND oc:size with only mount-root filtering.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: show my 25 biggest individual files anywhere in my storage ... folders other people shared with me and external storages ... must never appear in the biggest-files list
traps.mechanism: WebDAV SEARCH scoped to /files/<uid> searches every mount's cache (lib/private/Files/Cache/QuerySearchHelper.php:233-243), so the obvious size-ordered query returns shared and external files. Filtering them out client-side after nresults=25 silently yields fewer than 25 even when the user owns many more files; filtering by owner === me keeps files on personal/admin external storages (owner is the current user). The repo has a server-side switch: a top-level <d:eq> on oc:owner-id with the current uid is removed from the query and sets limitToHome (apps/dav/lib/Files/FileSearchBackend.php:349-357, extractWhereValue 516-556), which then skips all other mounts (QuerySearchHelper.php:233); it is only allowed with the home root as scope (lib/private/Files/Node/Folder.php:212-215). Alternatively paginate with firstresult until 25 own files are collected.
traps.why_unsignposted: No frontend SEARCH body uses oc:owner-id (WebDavSearch.ts, Recent.ts, @nextcloud/files getRecentSearch); the limitToHome behaviour is only visible in dav PHP.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: A mocked search response returns exactly the files the test expects; the shortfall only appears when big shared files occupy the top of the real ordering.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Have a few very large files in a share received by the user plus 30+ own files: the list shows fewer than 25 entries, or lists external-storage files. In code: limit 25 then client-side filtering, no owner-id condition or pagination.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Hidden files do count, even if I've hidden them in the list.
traps.mechanism: If the breakdown is built as a Files view (Navigation.register + getContents, the natural pattern from views/recent.ts), FilesList applies every registered list filter, including HiddenFilesFilter, which drops dotfiles and nc:hidden nodes (live-photo companion videos) whenever show_hidden is off (apps/files/src/filters/HiddenFilesFilter.ts:29-34, registered globally in init.ts:66). Those items silently vanish from the breakdown and the biggest-files list even though they use quota.
traps.why_unsignposted: The filter is registered globally without a view check and nothing in the View API indicates it applies to new views.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Unit tests call getContents directly and never pass through the FilesList filter pipeline.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: With show hidden files off, put a large dotfile or live-photo pair in the root and check whether it appears and counts.

other_criteria: Quota entry in the navigation opens the view
Items sorted biggest first, with formatted size and percentage of used space
Clicking a folder drills down with the same rules
Top 25 biggest files across own storage
Shared-with-me and external storage content never counted or listed
ideas.frontend_share: About 100% frontend: NavigationQuota.vue plus a new component/view and a service in apps/files/src using existing WebDAV PROPFIND/SEARCH and, optionally, the OCS shares API and files_external user mount endpoints. No backend change needed.
ideas.risks: The prompt's 'even when I've moved a shared folder inside' hint may push a careful model to check how oc:size is computed and find View.php. A correct nested-mount correction is fairly heavy (mount lists from several APIs), so a reviewer might see the requirement as large. quota_include_external_storage=true makes external storage count toward used, which contradicts the user's assumption on such servers (default config is fine). The stats endpoint is cached for 5 minutes (ApiController.php:368-369), so percentages against 'used' can be slightly stale right after changes. Group/team folders are not in this repo, so their mount type is not testable here.

ideas.title: Duplicate an external storage mount (admin and personal settings)
ideas.prompt: We have lots of SMB and SFTP external storages that are identical except for the share or folder. In Administration > External storage, could you add a 'Duplicate' button next to Edit on each mount? It should open the normal dialog pre-filled from that mount so I only change what differs and hit Create. People who can add personal external storages should get the same button for their own mounts in their personal settings. Once saved, the copy has to connect exactly like the original does; I don't want to discover broken mounts later. And it must show up for its users as an additional folder: never let me save a copy under a folder name another mount already uses for the same people, otherwise one of them silently disappears.
ideas.background: External storage settings were rewritten as a Vue 3 app (apps/files_external/src, 2026): ExternalStorageTableRow.vue renders each mount with Edit/Delete; Edit spawns AddExternalStorageDialog.vue with the storage object, and the Pinia store (store/storages.ts) calls POST/PUT on apps/files_external/globalstorages or userstorages. The dialog renders backend and auth-mechanism configuration fields (ConfigurationEntry.vue), with a custom element for RSA key auth (views/AuthMechanismRsa.vue). The feature adds a Duplicate action that pre-fills the dialog from an existing mount and creates a new one.
ideas.gap_evidence: git grep -i 'duplicate|clone' in apps/files_external/src at pin and origin/master a3222e16 only finds structuredClone in AddExternalStorageDialog.vue:43/46; ExternalStorageTableRow.vue offers only Edit and Delete. Commits to apps/files_external/src since the pin (252b3f27ef, 9b6afa9bba, 956e18a3cc, 86d67d3a58, a8552c962b, d5905ac909) are fixes. No '__unmodified__' handling exists anywhere in apps/files_external/src at either commit.
ideas.natural_implementation: Add a Duplicate NcButton in ExternalStorageTableRow.vue next to Edit (same visibility condition isAdmin || storage.type === 'personal'); onDuplicate: const { id, status, statusMessage, ...rest } = structuredClone(toRaw(props.storage)); spawnDialog(AddExternalStorageDialog, { storage: { ...rest, mountPoint: rest.mountPoint + ' (copy)' } }); on close call store.createGlobalStorage or store.createUserStorage depending on type. Optionally validate the new mountPoint against store.globalStorages/userStorages with a string comparison before saving.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: Once saved, the copy has to connect exactly like the original does; I don't want to discover broken mounts later.
traps.mechanism: The storages API never returns secrets: jsonSerialize(true) calls formatStorageForUI(), which replaces every VALUE_PASSWORD option with DefinitionParameter::UNMODIFIED_PLACEHOLDER '__unmodified__' (apps/files_external/lib/Lib/StorageConfig.php:385-393, 421-433; DefinitionParameter.php:17-18). Edit works because updateStorage skips placeholder values (apps/files_external/lib/Service/StoragesService.php:386), but addStorage writes every backend option verbatim (StoragesService.php:209-210). A duplicate pre-filled from the store shows a filled, 'required'-satisfied password field and saves the literal string '__unmodified__' as the SMB/SFTP password or S3 secret. For SFTP with RSA keys the private_key is a hidden password-type parameter (apps/files_external/lib/Lib/Auth/PublicKey/RSA.php:32-35), so the copy saves a placeholder key the user cannot even see; it needs regenerated keys (AuthMechanismRsa.vue generateKeys) or an explicit re-entry step.
traps.why_unsignposted: No frontend file references the placeholder; the edit dialog round-trips it invisibly, so the store data looks like real credentials. The server accepts the create without error; the mount only fails at status check or use.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Store/dialog tests use mocked storages with real-looking passwords and assert the POST body equals the pre-filled values, which encodes the wrong assumption.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Duplicate a password-authenticated mount without retyping the password: the POST body contains password '__unmodified__' and the new row turns red/unauthorized. For RSA, check the private_key in the POST.

traps.requirement_in_prompt: never let me save a copy under a folder name another mount already uses for the same people, otherwise one of them silently disappears
traps.mechanism: The server normalizes mount points on save (StorageConfig::setMountPoint -> Filesystem::normalizePath, StorageConfig.php:155-157), and mounts for a user are keyed by mount point, so a later one silently replaces an earlier one (lib/private/Files/Mount/Manager.php:39-45; apps/files_external/lib/Config/ConfigAdapter.php:168-180 builds $mounts[$mountPoint]; UserGlobalStoragesService::getUniqueStorages 71-99 picks one by priority). Stored values look like '/Projects', while users type 'Projects' or 'Projects/', so a plain string comparison never detects the clash. Applicability also matters: empty applicableUsers/applicableGroups means all users, so a copy collides with any same-named mount for overlapping users or groups; on the personal page, a personal mount also collides with a system mount applicable to that user (both are in the store as userStorages and globalStorages).
traps.why_unsignposted: The frontend never normalizes or compares mount points; nothing in the dialog warns about collisions and the server returns 201 for a clashing mount.
traps.why_tests_miss_it: Tests compare equal strings typed the same way, so the normalization and 'all users' cases are never exercised.
traps.how_reviewer_checks: Duplicate '/Projects' and type 'Projects' or 'Projects/' as the new name (all users), or duplicate a mount limited to group A while another mount with that name targets all users: the save is allowed and one mount disappears from the users' Files.

other_criteria: Duplicate button next to Edit for admins and for personal mounts
Dialog opens in create mode pre-filled with backend, auth mechanism, options, mount options, applicable users/groups and priority
Created via the correct endpoint (global vs personal) and appears in the table
ideas.frontend_share: 100% frontend: ExternalStorageTableRow.vue, AddExternalStorageDialog.vue (create-mode prefill, required secret handling), store/storages.ts, optional validation helper. No backend change.
ideas.risks: The prompt's 'connect exactly like the original' may lead a strong model to inspect the GET payload or StorageConfig::jsonSerialize and find the placeholder. The collision rule needs group membership the admin UI does not know, so a reviewer might accept over-blocking any same-named mount, which weakens the second trap. Admins cannot see users' personal mounts, so some collisions are undetectable from the admin page. Overall it is the smallest and most findable of the three ideas.

rejected_ideas: Pre-upload quota check: FilesList.vue:436 already uses the current folder's quota-available-bytes; the special negative values are common knowledge, so the traps are signposted.
Undo-delete toast: finding the item in the trash is spec-like; deleteAction labels ('Leave this share', 'Disconnect storage', 'Delete permanently') point straight at the special cases.

Bulk share selected files: wrong permissions for files and folders fail loudly on the server; SharePermissionsToolBox and the sidebar show the file vs folder permission bundles; the sharing UI is also being rewritten upstream.
Expiry column / bulk extend in Shares views: enforcement settings are fully exposed in ConfigService.ts; only the duplicate-merge quirk is silent.
Bulk 'stop sharing' in Shared with others: only one silent trap (merge keeps the first share id), and the prompt has to mention multiple shares.
Ctrl+C/X/V clipboard for files: handleCopyMoveNodesTo already covers conflicts, moving into itself and permissions; a model would just reuse it.
Drag onto folder-tree entries: BreadCrumbs.vue:251-320 already implements drop with permission and copy logic to copy from.
Merge folders on move/copy conflict: an algorithmic, well-specified task; Sabre overwrite semantics are well known.
File list tag filter: already implemented upstream (4f59ce6829).
Folder item counts via nc:contained-file-count: only one trap (counts include hidden files), and a correct fix needs a listing per folder.
Trashbin 'expires in N days': retention config is not exposed to the frontend, so it needs backend work.
Reminders overview view: there is no list endpoint, so it needs backend work.
Recent including newly uploaded old files (upload_time/last_activity): server semantics are murky and last_activity is not sortable.
Owner column: a single trap (uid_owner vs uid_file_owner in SharingService).
LDAP config duplicate: already exists (ServerTab 'Copy current configuration').
Waffle app menu option: a layout-only change with no gradable silent traps.
Current-folder quota in the navigation (#36457): the stats API already accepts ?dir=, so there is little hidden logic.
Version diff/compare and 'keep last N versions': the existing isCurrent and named-version handling signposts the traps.
User status custom clear time / user timezone: the existing code already uses getFirstDay; the timezone trap would have to be spelled out in the prompt.

evaluations.title: Per-room 'Ignore @room' notification switch
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. At the pin, RoomNotifs.ts setRoomNotifsStateMuted adds an override rule with rule_id = roomId (comment: 'using the room ID as the rule ID is logical'). findOverrideMuteRule / isRuleMaybeRoomMuteRule only match rules with one room_id condition, so a two-condition @room rule under a different id survives mute and unmute. The 'XXX: We have to assume the default is to notify for all messages' comment is at RoomNotifs.ts:75. The precedence claim (user override rules beat server-default is_user_mention and content-kind keyword rules) is standard Matrix spec. I did not re-read pushprocessor.ts in the js-sdk.
evaluations.refutation: Every trap comes from Matrix push-rule precedence, which is public spec that Opus knows well: kinds run override > content > room > sender > underride, and user overrides sit above server defaults. The prompt also names every case: direct mention, keyword, all-messages vs mentions-only, muted before vs after, other apps. A model turning each sentence into a push rule will add higher-priority exceptions for m.mentions.user_ids and per-keyword rules, make the @room rule's actions depend on the room level, and add the legacy body '@room' rule because the prompt says 'other apps'. The rule-id collision trap (3a) only fires if the model reuses roomId, which is unlikely since a PUT would visibly overwrite the mute rule. 'Whether I muted it before or after' points straight at insertion order. Trap 4 is admittedly signposted by pill.tsx and VectorPushRulesDefinitions.
evaluations.fairness_issues: This is mostly spec-following, which the brief warns against. Default-level rooms copying account underride actions (one_to_one with sound) is beyond what the prompt states. Keeping per-room keyword exceptions in sync when keywords change later is implied but never stated. Grading needs two accounts with @room permission and a raw legacy event. Trap 4 is self-declared weak. The fully correct answer is a combinatorial rule set that a reviewer could call over-demanding.
evaluations.fixes: No fix is worth making: the precedence semantics are public spec, and the prompt has to name each case to be fair, which gives away the traps.

evaluations.title: Previous/next navigation in the image viewer (lightbox)
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. FilePanel renders <ScopedRoomContextProvider {...this.context} timelineRenderingType={File}>, so liveTimeline is still the room's. Only RoomView (1485/1494) and ThreadView (430) set liveTimeline. FilePanel builds its own filtered timeline set (fetchFileEventsServer). MImageBody.onClick opens a one-image Modal.createDialog. useMediaVisible order is explicit reveal, then own events, then mediaPreviewConfig Off/On/Private by join rule. All of this matches.
evaluations.refutation: The prompt names every source (timeline, thread, Files panel, jump-to-date or permalink), so a strong model will investigate how each one gets its events. Reading FilePanel shows its separate timelineSet right away. getTimelineForEvent, or passing TimelinePanel's timelineSet/window down through a context, handles traps 1 and 2 together because they share a cause. useMediaVisible is a short, readable hook referenced by MImageBody's props, and the prompt mentions media preview settings, so the model will copy its logic or wrap each slide in a function component. Rebinding props to the current image (trap 4) is routine refactoring that any strong model does once it adds index state.
evaluations.fairness_issues: The feature is large, so a reviewer may read misses as incompleteness rather than traps. Files panel in encrypted rooms on web depends on Seshat, which is a confound. On-screen arrows are layout and cannot be graded. Paging past the loaded window for a filtered timeline set adds scope.
evaluations.fixes: Traps 1 and 2 collapse into one root cause and trap 4 is not silent. Only Files-panel sourcing plus visibility would remain, which is too few independent silent traps.

evaluations.title: POS 'Exchange' at the till: return items and sell replacements on one ticket
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held at pin e3e47d97. onDoRefund sets is_refund=true and copies pricelist_id/fiscal_position_id. getRefundLinesDetails copies price_unit/discount/tax_ids with price_type 'automatic'. pos_discount patches onDoRefund to call applyDiscount on the destination order, and its PosStore.setup registers a pos.order.line 'update' listener that re-applies globalDiscountPc over every isGlobalDiscountApplicable line (only tip and discount products excluded). createNewOrder forces config pricelist and default FP even with partner_id; setPartner -> updatePricelistAndFiscalPosition is the only customer-pricelist path; selectPartner refuses on orders with refund lines. isRefund is is_refund===true; product_screen blocks numpad for isRefund; payment_screen auto-invoice is keyed on isRefund. pos_order.py move_type is out_refund if is_refund or total<0, with qty_sign flipping. pos_loyalty _getDiscountableOnOrder sums all getOrderlines() including refund lines; only _get_regular_order_lines excludes them. Odoo master e04968ab (2026-11-04) has no 'exchange' in ticket_screen.js/.xml, pos_order.js or pos_order.py.
evaluations.refutation: Odoo developers habitually grep for patches of a method they change. Grepping onDoRefund lists the pos_discount patch, and applyDiscount sits in the same file just below setup(), whose listener is plainly visible. The prompt's 'changing quantities as usual' and 'invoiced like a refund' will send the model to every isRefund usage, where it may set is_refund=false and extend the auto-invoice condition explicitly. 'Fresh sale for that customer' should make it call setPartner or set the customer's pricelist instead of copying the original's. A model that also reads pos_loyalty's reward builders could exclude refunded lines. Counter-point: catching all four needs reasoning across three modules plus the Python invoice path, and none can be checked without a DB with pos_discount/pos_loyalty data, which the model is unlikely to set up. Each trap has roughly a 40-55% miss rate.
evaluations.fairness_issues: The back-office 'Return Products then add lines' flow is arguably related prior art, but it is not at the till. One order holds a single fiscal position/pricelist, so when the customer's current FP differs from the original's, refund-line taxes and new-line taxes pull in different directions; reviewers should avoid FP-change cases. Expected values with loyalty need careful reviewer setup (create the promotion after the original sale). The pricelist trap has both failure modes (copy vs don't copy), which is good, but the reviewer must test both scenarios. Grading needs pos_discount and pos_loyalty installed.
evaluations.fixes: Keep the prompt. Tell reviewers to use the same fiscal position for original and exchange and to create promotions after the original sale. Grade the invoice outcome and the numpad outcome, not line-sign display.

evaluations.title: Meal-voucher payment method that may only pay for food categories
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. pos.category _load_pos_data_domain with limit_categories loads only ids in iface_available_categ_ids (plus printer categories), using 'in' rather than child_of, so parents are absent. product_template's domain is the same. payment_screen.updateSelectedPaymentline caps amount only when the config has no cash method. The fast-payment comment block and fastPaymentMethod = config.payment_method_ids[0] exist in pos_store (~2451-2465). pos_discount discount lines are on discount_product_id.
evaluations.refutation: The prompt names every trap source: line discounts, the global discount button, promotion and loyalty, gift card and eWallet as payment, no change, one-tap buttons, and tills limited to some categories. A strong model will grep each one. 'One-tap payment buttons' leads straight to fastValidate/validateOrderFast, and 'only some categories' leads to limit_categories loading in Python, where the missing parents are obvious. Gift-card lines are recognizable by program_type and the code comment 'These are considered payments'. The remaining real difficulty is attributing loyalty rewards to items (free-product and specific/cheapest rewards), which the model can do from reward_id.discount_applicability and reward_product_ids.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Allocating order-wide reductions per item is open-ended (proportional is the reading for global %, but mixed cases are debatable). The tip-on-voucher-line path is a product decision. It needs backend fields, a small but real non-frontend part. An OCA pos_meal_voucher module is prior art outside the repo. Grading needs pos_discount and pos_loyalty with specific programs.
evaluations.fixes: Limit graded reduction cases to the clear ones: global %, buy-2-get-1 free on food, a promo on non-food only, and a gift card. Drop the tip path. Consider removing the 'restricted tills' hint and the 'one-tap' hint from the prompt only if those outcomes can still be stated, for example 'however the cashier pays'.

evaluations.title: 'Order again': start a new ticket from a past order for the same customer
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. handleComboProduct only builds children when configure=true (popup) or opts.comboOpts is given (pos_store ~1079-1107, comment 'In case of clicking a combo product a popup will be shown'). createNewOrder forces config pricelist and FP regardless of partner_id. The _getEmptyOrder pattern uses addNewOrder({partner_id}).
evaluations.refutation: The prompt says 'their pricelist and tax setup', so the model will look for how a customer's pricelist gets applied and find setPartner -> updatePricelistAndFiscalPosition. The most common API for adding lines is setOrder + addLineToCurrentOrder, which pos_loyalty patches, so the promotions trap is avoided by default. The prompt lists the special line types (discounts, rewards, tips, gift cards), so the model filters on is_reward_line / isDiscountLine / isTipLine. Only the combo configure=false behaviour and gift-card trigger products remain plausibly silent.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Lower business value. The prompt's explicit list of excluded line types gives that trap away. It overlaps mechanically with the exchange idea (createNewOrder pricelist), so it is not independent.
evaluations.fixes: None worth doing. Fold the createNewOrder-pricelist insight into the Exchange idea instead.

evaluations.title: Use the profile time zone (not the browser's) for every time the web app shows or lets you pick
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. timerender.ts:23 display_time_zone = browser_time_zone(). set_display_time_zone has the comment 'Exported for testing only; we do not support live-updating the time zone'. initialize() falls back to user_settings.timezone only for undefined/Etc/Unknown. scheduled_messages.compute_send_times uses setDate/getDay/setHours and get_filtered_send_opts uses date.getDay()/getHours(). flatpickr.ts passes defaultDate through and uses formatDate: formatISO(date). user_profile.ts renders DATE fields with parseISO(value) through timerender.
evaluations.refutation: The prompt names every area: send-later presets and their availability, the custom picker, global-time insertion, live updates, and date-only profile fields. All share one generic, well-known cause: browser-local Date methods. A strong model will grep web/src for getHours|setHours|getDay|getDate|parseISO|flatpickr and convert each hit with TZDate/{in: display_tz}. Shifting flatpickr in and out with date-fns-tz is a standard pattern Opus knows. The date-only field is explicitly called out, so the model will format it as UTC or parse it in the zone.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Grading needs a browser-zone override. Whether /stats and other pages count is ambiguous. The traps are not independent (one sweep fixes most). Upstream wants a privacy discussion (#16958), which does not affect grading.
evaluations.fixes: Cannot fix without dropping the area names from the prompt, which would make the rules unstated.

evaluations.title: Silence desktop pop-ups and sounds for mentions of chosen user groups
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. message_store.ts maps mentioned_me_directly: convert_flag('mentioned') and mentioned = mentioned || stream_wildcard || topic_wildcard. message_send.py:692 says 'For single user as well as user group mentions, we set the mentioned flag'. message_notifications.ts:246 says '@-<username> mentions take precedence over muted-ness' and returns true on mentioned_me_directly. The 'wildcard mentions' branches in should_send_desktop_notification test message.mentioned. message_list_view.ts:629 holds the giveaway comment 'Currently the API does not differentiate between a group mention and a user mention'. Server-side group_mentioned is only read in message_edit/narrow, never set on send.
evaluations.refutation: Opus may remember from the Zulip API docs that the 'mentioned' flag covers group mentions. A model has to parse content for .user-group-mention anyway, and it may parse .user-mention:not(.silent) for 'mentions me by name' instead of trusting the flag. When it reads message_store to see what mentioned_me_directly is, it sees the same underlying flag feeding both fields, which invites the question. Traps 1-3 are correlated: a model that computes 'effective flags with silenced groups removed' and then reruns the normal logic gets all three. Trap 4 (quotes) is stated explicitly and .silent is easy to find.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Per-browser storage is unusual but requested. Group membership via subgroups needs recursive checks. Traps 1-3 share one root cause, so a reviewer may count them as one. Grading needs two accounts and a group.
evaluations.fixes: Add an independent second trap so failure does not depend only on the flag conflation, for example an existing notification path that bypasses message_notifications (compose echo or edits re-notifying), or drop trap 4 and accept a thinner idea. As it stands this is a single-root-cause task.

evaluations.title: Sync web drafts with the server drafts API (pending web implementation)
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. zerver/actions/user_settings.py:604-609 deletes all Draft rows when enable_drafts_synchronization goes False 'but don't send delete events'. No /json/drafts usage exists in web/src at the pin.
evaluations.refutation: This mostly follows a documented API. Each reconciliation trap is stated as a requirement (offline delete, rename follows, re-enable uploads, sent draft gone), and a strong model designs for each: storing server ids and pruning local drafts whose id is missing from the register state, grepping rename_stream_recipient for moves, clearing server ids or re-uploading everything on re-enable as the prompt literally says ('upload whatever drafts are on this computer'). The send-race orphan is timing-dependent and only gradable by reading the diff.
evaluations.fairness_issues: The 1000-draft register cap makes 'absent means deleted' slightly unsound, but it is not gradable. The orphan race is racy. The feature is mostly API wiring.

evaluations.title: Web vault 'Duplicate logins' report with one-click Merge
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. cipher.service.ts encrypt() calls adjustCipherHistory first, which loads the stored cipher when it has an id. updateModelfromExistingCipher starts with model.passwordHistory = existingCipher.passwordHistory || [] and then prepends only the item's own old password. CipherRequest sends attachments only as id-keyed metadata (attachments/attachments2 maps). canDeleteCipher$ returns cipher.permissions?.delete. vault.component.ts bulk delete uses ciphers.every(c => c.edit). The reused-passwords report filters on edit/viewPassword.
evaluations.refutation: adjustCipherHistory is the first statement in encrypt() and has a JSDoc ('Adjusts the cipher history ... based on the original cipher'). A model saving a hand-built history will very likely read it and the private updater it calls, so the history overwrite is partly signposted. Opus knows Bitwarden attachments are encrypted blobs tied to one item (and to its cipher key), and shareAttachmentWithServer is an in-repo download/re-encrypt/re-upload template. 'Allowed to delete the copies' invites a grep for canDelete, which finds canDeleteCipher$. Only the passwordRevisionDate-null fallback (use creationDate, not revisionDate) is truly quiet.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Grouping items with several URIs is ambiguous (do not grade it). The collections union is signposted by a comment (criterion only). Uploading before the PUT may hit server 'out of date' behaviour. The 'newest password' rule relies on the reviewer agreeing that a never-changed password dates from creation, which is inferable from cipher.view passwordRevisionDisplayDate but slightly arguable. The feature is large.
evaluations.fixes: Keep the attachments, delete-permission and password-age traps, and treat history as a bonus, since it is somewhat signposted. Tighten the prompt's 'changed most recently' to 'whichever password is newest (a password never changed counts from when the item was created)' only if that does not give the trap away. Otherwise accept it as is and rank it below the top 3.

evaluations.title: Import option 'Update existing items' instead of creating duplicates
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. import.service.ts filters importResult.ciphers for restricted types without remapping folderRelationships/collectionRelationships (an existing latent bug). handleIndividualImport/handleOrganizationalImport send KvpRequest(r[0], r[1]) unchanged. encrypt's adjustCipherHistory overwrite is the same as in the merge idea.
evaluations.refutation: The prompt says unmatched items 'must still land in the folders or collections the file puts them in', which sends the model straight to the relationship arrays printed a few lines below in handleIndividualImport. Their [cipherIndex, folderIndex] shape is obvious, so it will remap. The history trap is the same partly signposted adjustCipherHistory as in the merge idea. 'Couldn't change that item's password from the normal edit screen' points at the edit form's viewPassword gating.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Not independent of the merge idea (same history mechanism). Which items count for Admin Console org imports is ambiguous. Only two strong traps, both hinted.
evaluations.fixes: None. Keep only the Merge idea from this repo.

evaluations.title: Live counts for Starred / Archived / Trash / Untagged and custom smart views that match the list exactly
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held (pin = origin HEAD, 2026-11-02). ItemManager.setPrimaryItemDisplayOptions calls rebuildSystemSmartViews({...options, ...override}), and the Trash override forces includeArchived=true. SmartViewBuilder bakes includeArchived/Protected/Pinned/Trashed clauses into system predicates. computeFiltersForDisplayOptions skips include options whose keypath the predicate already mentions. notesMatchingSmartView passes only {views:[view]} and iterates Note only. The starred predicate has no archived clause and the untagged predicate has no trashed clause.
evaluations.refutation: The prompt demands 'exactly how many items I'd see in that list', which sends a strong model to replicate the list pipeline: ItemListController.reloadDisplayPreferences -> setPrimaryItemDisplayOptions. There it sees the Trash/Archived overrides and the rebuildSystemSmartViews call, and may decide to build a per-view ItemDisplayController with BuildSmartViews(viewOptions) plus vault options, which fixes traps 1-3 together. Vaults, files and live updates are all named, so the model will look for vault display options and preference/vault events. Counter: notesMatchingSmartView is the obvious, spec-blessed helper (used by trashedItems and ItemManager.spec), and the 'cached system view predicates were built for another view' fact is very easy to miss.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Counts already exist for Notes/Files/Conflicts, so a reviewer may see it as extending an existing feature (acceptable, since the views listed have none). Traps 1 and 2 are correlated. The vault check needs Labs vaults. Live-update grading must be done in the browser but is quick.
evaluations.fixes: Drop the vault clause (Labs-only, and named in the prompt anyway) and keep cached-predicate (trap 1), missing include filters (trap 2), and files plus live star/pref updates (trap 4) as the graded set. Consider adding one concrete user-visible example to the reviewer guide (archived+trashed note counted in Trash).

evaluations.title: Find and replace across all notes
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. SuperEditor's inner-value observer only reloads Lexical when isPayloadSourceRetrieved(source). PlainEditor resets only for retrieved sources or editor/noteType changes. RemoteRetrieved appears in web/src only at NoteHistoryController.ts:346.
evaluations.refutation: The prompt says 'including in the note I have open right now', so the model will open NoteView/SuperEditor/PlainEditor observers and read the isPayloadSourceRetrieved guard. Copying restoreRevision's RemoteRetrieved emit is then natural. 'The notes list should show the updated text' leads to preview_plain/preview_html in ListItemNotePreviewText. 'Not allowed to edit' leads to a grep for readonly, which finds isCurrentUserReadonlyVaultMember. The noteType trap is contested by SuperNoteImporter's lenient handling.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Trap 4 is contested. Trap 3 needs Labs shared vaults and a second account. Every trap is hinted by a prompt sentence.
evaluations.fixes: None that keeps the rules stated.

evaluations.title: Copy a note into a (shared) vault, keeping the original private
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held for tags. MutatorService.findOrCreateTag(title, createInVault) -> findOrCreateTagByTitle -> itemManager.findTagByTitleAndParent, which searches getRootTags() by title regardless of vault. The vault is used only when creating. I did not re-check the file-duplication valet-token path.
evaluations.refutation: 'My original note and its files must keep working exactly as before, whatever later happens to the copy' prompts a model to check whether duplicateItem shares file blobs (it copies remoteIdentifier), and it will re-upload through FilesController.uploadNewFile. 'Look identical including embedded images' plus 'others need to open them' leads to remapping snfile fileUuid in the Super JSON. moveItemToVault's 'linked to other items' refusal surfaces the duplicateItem reference problem loudly during any manual run. The tag lookup ignoring the vault is the only quietly silent trap.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Vaults are a Labs feature. Full verification needs two accounts and a shared vault. Trap 4 fails loudly (an alert), so it is not silent.

evaluations.title: Read-only and No-download badges on Files rows, consistent across All files and the Shares views
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held strongly. @nextcloud/files 4.0.0 (the locked version) declares Permission.CREATE: 4 and Permission.WRITE: 4 ('Can change the file content') and UPDATE: 2 ('move, rename'). parsePermissions maps 'W' -> WRITE, 'CK' -> CREATE, 'NV' -> UPDATE. DavUtil.php adds N for movable mount roots via canRename and computes W from the root cache entry, with the comment 'since we always add update permissions for the root of movable mounts'. View.php adds UPDATE|DELETE to MoveableMount roots. SharingService.ts uses permissions: item_permissions || permissions (OCS server constants: 2 = content update, 4 = create). It merges duplicates with groupBy(...).map(nodes => nodes[0]), only combining share-types. ShareAPIController: own share item_permissions = node perms; recipient side = share perms | DELETE | (UPDATE if canEditShare). Neighbouring helpers point both ways: isSyncable uses Permission.WRITE, while FileInfo.canEdit, FileEntryMixin and renameAction use Permission.UPDATE.
evaluations.refutation: A model that reads the d.ts will use WRITE for files and CREATE for folders, which is right for DAV. The prompt's explicit 'same badges ... under Shares' and the Anna direct-plus-group example push it into SharingService. There Opus, who knows OCS share constants, may notice that item_permissions bit 2 is content-update while DAV bit 2 is rename. It could then refetch DAV props for Shares-view nodes, which fixes the OCS, merge and outgoing-attribute traps in one move. An owner === me early return (strongly suggested by 'files in my own storage never get one') neutralises the outgoing-attributes trap and the own-file half of the OCS trap. Counter: any single-bit predicate necessarily fails either the DAV mount-root case or the OCS received-edit case, and the merge keeping nodes[0] breaks the direct-plus-group example in Shared with you whichever bit is used.
evaluations.fairness_issues: The OCS-permission trap and the outgoing-attribute trap share a root cause (Shares views are OCS-built), so a reviewer may count them as one. 'Same as when I open it' relies on DAV permissions as ground truth, since editors are not in the repo. Grid-view rendering is not gradable. Upstream is reworking the sharing sidebar behind a flag, but SharingService semantics are unchanged at HEAD per the idea. Otherwise all rules are stated, the feature is missing and the work is frontend-only.
evaluations.fixes: Grade three independent outcomes: (1) a directly shared view-only file in All files, (2) a received editable file in Shared with you, (3) the direct-view-only-plus-group-edit example in Shared with you. Treat outgoing-attribute No-download as a criterion, not a counted trap.

evaluations.title: 'What's using my space' storage breakdown opened from the quota entry in Files
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. View::getDirectoryContent adds nested mount root sizes to the containing child folder ('mountpoint inside subfolder add size to the correct folder'). FileSearchBackend extracts an oc:owner-id equality equal to the current uid and sets limitHome (and throws for other uids).
evaluations.refutation: The prompt says 'even when I've moved a shared folder inside one of my own folders', which pushes a careful model to question what oc:size includes and possibly find View.php. A strong model may sidestep both traps by computing everything from a SEARCH and summing client-side from own-storage files, or by paging the search until it has 25 own files. The hidden-files filter only applies if the model builds a registered Files view rather than a modal.
evaluations.fairness_issues: A fully correct nested-mount correction is heavy (it needs mount lists from several APIs). quota_include_external_storage changes semantics. The stats cache causes 5-minute staleness. limitToHome is obscure enough that a reviewer might accept pagination plus filtering.
evaluations.fixes: None that adds a second independent silent trap.

evaluations.title: Duplicate an external storage mount (admin and personal settings)
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. StorageConfig formatStorageForUI replaces VALUE_PASSWORD options with UNMODIFIED_PLACEHOLDER. StoragesService.updateStorage skips placeholder values, but addStorage writes every backend option verbatim. apps/files_external/src has no placeholder handling.
evaluations.refutation: 'Has to connect exactly like the original' makes a strong model check what the GET returns. Opus likely knows Nextcloud masks secrets as '__unmodified__', so it will clear password fields and require re-entry or RSA key regeneration. Mount-point collision is stated explicitly, and normalising leading/trailing slashes is an obvious step.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Collision detection needs group membership the admin UI may not know, and admins cannot see users' personal mounts, so the second trap is partly undeterminable. It is small.

evaluations.title: Per-panel time range and refresh interval on dashboards
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held at pin cbcfe2fa. ppl_search_interceptor.ts injects this.queryService.timefilter.timefilter.getTime() into request.params.body.timeRange and builds the WHERE time clause from the global timefilter, and getAggConfig also reads global time. search_service routes enhanced-language requests to languageConfig.search.search. Timeline buildOptions uses timefilter.getBounds() for the x-axis interval and format, and the component passes opensearchDashboards.services.timefilter. Timeline brushing emits applyFilter with timeFieldName '*'. getAutoRefreshFetch$ subscriptions exist in explore_embeddable.tsx:166, search_embeddable.tsx:159 and visualize_embeddable. Only a leftover 'CUSTOM_TIME_RANGE' string exists in dashboard_container.tsx.
evaluations.refutation: A thorough model could grep all timefilter.getTime()/getBounds()/getAutoRefreshFetch$ usages and reach all four traps in one sweep. 'Refresh only on that schedule' points at the global auto-refresh subscriptions, and 'drag-to-zoom just that panel' for listed TSVB/Timeline may lead it to their brush handlers. Kibana's 2019 x-pack commit in history gives the core action, badge and flyout design. Counter: OSD has dozens of timefilter reads. The PPL path hides behind searchSource -> search service -> language interceptor, while the explore embeddable visibly uses input.timeRange and looks correct. Timeline's data path is correct, so the model stops there. Auto-refresh must be suppressed in four separate embeddable classes. None of this is checkable without OpenSearch plus the SQL plugin. Traps sit in distinct code paths, so they are not one root cause.
evaluations.fairness_issues: The prompt is about 165 words, slightly over the limit, and bundles time range and refresh interval (a reviewer could call it two features). PPL verification needs query enhancements, the explore plugin and the OpenSearch SQL plugin, though reading the diff is enough. Upstream HEAD later added an explicit timeRange override in the PPL interceptor (not at the pin), which confirms the fix shape. Brushing traps partly overlap (both are about global time being changed).
evaluations.fixes: Trim the prompt under 160 words, for example by dropping 'same quick ranges and date format' and the badge detail. Keep the four stated outcomes: PPL panels, Timeline axis labels, refresh-only-on-own-schedule, and TSVB/Timeline drag-to-zoom. Tell reviewers to grade PPL by diff reading if no SQL plugin is available.

evaluations.title: 'View in Discover' action for dashboard panels
evaluations.evidence_holds: Held. DiscoverUrlGenerator builds `${appBasePath}#/${savedSearchId}`. migrateUrlState only recognises '#/view/:id' for saved searches, so '#/<id>' falls to the bare '#/' pattern with no id. use_search.ts:556 replaces the saved search's query with the URL query whenever the URL query is not the default.
evaluations.refutation: 'Hit count in Discover matches what the panel counts' makes a strong model realise Discover has one query slot, so the saved search's query and the dashboard query must be combined, one of them as a filter. Any manual or code-level check of the URL it generates against Discover's route table exposes the '#/<id>' problem. The TSVB/Vega exclusion and the 'both view and edit mode' rule are stated explicitly, so the model will exclude by vis type name and drop Kibana's view-mode gate. Those two traps are effectively not traps.
evaluations.fairness_issues: Only two real silent traps, both in Discover's loader rather than in the feature path. A reviewer may call them pre-existing Discover quirks. The edit-mode trap is self-rated weak.
evaluations.fixes: None that adds a strong second trap.
